title: Drag repaints the whole run on a full-res canvas and re-renders the entire ShotViewer tree on every pointer move
claim: A move or resize drag repaints the entire run containing the mark (all of its siblings) on a full-resolution canvas. Each move also calls `editShapes` -> `setShapes` in ShotViewer, re-rendering the whole ~1650-line tree (sidebar, ColorPicker, ClipMeta).
fix: During a drag, lift the dragged mark into its own layer (as is already done for drafts) and throttle with rAF; memoise the side panel.

title: Failed thumbnail rebuild silently keeps the pre-edit (unredacted) thumbnail
claim: After an edit, thumbnail failure is only logged: `if let Err(err) = make_still(..) { log::warn!(..) }` (commands.rs:640-643), and `set_picture` (clips.rs:290-302) doesn't touch `thumb_path`. The old `thumbs/<id>.jpg` stays; gallery and console tiles use `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, which changes, so they re-fetch the old JPEG. Also, if the capture-time thumbnail failed, `thumb_path` stays NULL forever even after a successful rebuild.
fix: Build the thumbnail in-process from the `picture` already in memory (box downscale + the existing `png` crate; drop the ffmpeg dependency for stills). On any failure delete the old thumbnail and set `thumb_path` to NULL. Have `set_picture` also set `thumb_path`.

title: Editor trusts database dimensions when there is no original; received screenshots carry sender-claimed dimensions
claim: `screenshot_edit` falls back to `} else { (clip.width, clip.height) }` when there is no original (commands.rs:457-461). Received screenshots store sender-supplied meta as dimensions (`width: meta.width, height: meta.height`, share.rs:129-136, 841-851) without reading the file header.
fix: In `screenshot_edit` always use `size_of_png(clip.path)` when there is no original. At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and store the real dimensions.

title: Received screenshots may be JPEG, which permanently breaks editing and Copy picture
claim: The receive path accepts `jpg/jpeg` for screenshots (share.rs:1187-1190), but the editor and clipboard assume PNG.
fix: At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and reject non-PNG screenshots.

title: AnnotateLayer and CropLayer never clear an interrupted drag
claim: AnnotateLayer only handles pointer down/move/up (ShotAnnotate.tsx:917-925), and `onMove` never checks `event.buttons` (764-767); CropLayer (ShotViewer.tsx:1408-1414) has the same gap. The stage's own pan handler already handles the case ("Let go somewhere the stage never heard of it (Alt+Tab mid-drag)", ShotViewer.tsx:786-790), but the two layers don't.
fix: Add `onPointerCancel` and `onLostPointerCapture` handlers that reset `drag.current` and the draft, and ignore moves with `event.buttons === 0`.

title: Unredacted original kept forever in originals/<id>/image.png with no way to purge it
claim: The pre-edit original is stored at `%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\originals\<id>\image.png` (shot.rs:287-289) indefinitely. `discard_original` (edit.rs:139-151) only knows `video.mp4` and returns "There is no original to throw away." for screenshots, so the only way to purge the unredacted pixels is to delete the screenshot.
fix: Add a "Flatten - discard history" action that removes `image.png`, `base.png` and `shot.json` (keeping `under.*`). Mention in the UI that blur and crop stay reversible locally.

title: Undo merges drags across an AnnotateLayer remount because gesture ids restart at 0
claim: Gesture ids come from `gestures.current`, which restarts at 0 whenever AnnotateLayer remounts (draw -> crop -> Cancel -> draw), while `lastGesture` in ShotViewer survives the remount. The first drag afterwards (`drag-1`) therefore merges with the last drag before the remount (`drag-1`).
fix: Use a module-level or `useId`-based gesture counter and reset `lastGesture` on mode change.

title: Restyle undo key merges separate style changes into one undo step
claim: `restyle` uses the history key `style-${id}-${keys}`, which is identical for separate clicks on the same mark and property.
fix: Give restyle a per-interaction token (pointerdown or slider-start).

title: Hit-test margin uses blur size (a radius) as stroke width, creating a huge invisible halo
claim: `const margin = shape.tool === "text" ? slack : Math.max(slack, shape.size);` treats a blur's `size` as stroke width, but for blur it is a radius running up to `base*12` (96 px at 4K, 192 px at 8K).
fix: Use `slack` for blur (and text).

title: Blur edge handling differs between preview and file
claim: The preview's backdrop-filter clips and mirrors at the patch edge, while the Rust blur reads `radius` pixels beyond the patch. A saved blur cut by a crop reads black stage in the preview but real pixels in Rust.
fix: No specific fix given beyond aligning preview and file behaviour (see ED-1).

title: Caption text jumps vertically on commit (CSS line-height vs canvas textBaseline top)
claim: The caption edit field uses `lineHeight: 1.25` (CSS half-leading) while the canvas draws with `textBaseline = "top"` (em-box top), so the two place text at different vertical offsets.
fix: No specific fix given (align the field's line box with the canvas baseline).

title: Thumbnail ffmpeg filter fails or upscales for extreme crops
claim: The thumbnail filter is `-vf scale=480:-1`, fixing width at 480 regardless of aspect or source size.
fix: Use `scale='min(480,iw)':'min(480,ih)':force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease`.

title: Out-of-range rectangles are clamped to a 1-pixel strip instead of rejected
claim: Clamping uses `x.min(self.width.saturating_sub(1))`, so a rectangle entirely right of or below the picture becomes a 1-px strip at the edge: `clamped` and `crop` succeed and `blur` writes one column, instead of returning an error. The UI never sends such a rect, but a buggy or compromised caller could.
fix: `if area.x >= self.width || area.y >= self.height { return Err(..) }`.

title: No frontend tests
claim: There are no frontend test files or test runner, so editor logic such as `markRect`, `fitRatio`/`spanned`, `toSteps`, `shift`/`readMarks`, `sigmaOf` and the move-clamp in `onMove` is untested.
fix: Add vitest coverage for `markRect` vs fixtures from the Rust `rect_kept` tests, `fitRatio`/`spanned`, `toSteps`, `shift`/`readMarks` round-trip, `sigmaOf`, and the move-clamp in `onMove`.

title: Size slider steps from a fractional minimum, so values snap off the default
claim: The slider uses `step = 1` (Controls.tsx:95) with `range()` min `Math.max(1, base*0.4)` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:127), which can be fractional (e.g. 0.8 or 3.2), so values snap to 0.8, 1.8 …
fix: Pass `step = min` or round `min`.

title: crop's doc comment merged into clamped's doc; crop has none
claim: `crop`'s doc ("Cut a rectangle out of the picture…") is merged into `clamped`'s doc comment at shot.rs:34-47, and `crop` itself has no doc comment.
fix: Split the doc comment so each function documents itself.

title: clamped and crop duplicate the same clamping logic
claim: `clamped` and `crop` in shot.rs repeat the same clamping logic.
fix: `crop(Rect)` should take the already-clamped rect.

title: MAX_ZOOM_STEP duplicates MAX_ZOOM
claim: `MAX_ZOOM_STEP = 8` (ShotViewer.tsx:60) duplicates `MAX_ZOOM = 8` (pictureBox.ts:78).
fix: Use a single shared constant.

title: Watermark asset size 535x152 hard-coded in TS
claim: The watermark asset size 535x152 is hard-coded in watermark.ts:142-143.
fix: Derive the size from the asset (or share the constant with Rust).

title: Marks stored as JSON-in-JSON with full float precision
claim: shot.json stores the marks as a JSON string inside JSON (`Edit.marks: String`), and point coordinates are saved at full float precision (bloat).
fix: Use `serde_json::value::RawValue` for marks; round point coordinates.

title: Redaction blur written to the file is much weaker than the preview shows
claim: The saved PNG gets a single box-blur pass per axis (`blur_rows(&patch, &mut across, pw, ph, radius); … blur_rows(&turned, &mut done, ph, pw, radius);` in shot.rs), while the preview is a CSS Gaussian of the same variance (`backdropFilter: blur(${sigmaOf(step.radius) * box.scale}px)` with `Math.sqrt((radius*(radius+1))/3)` in ShotAnnotate.tsx). Matching variance does not match legibility: a box kernel has sinc side-lobes, a Gaussian none. For r = 4/8/16 (the 1080p minimum and default) the box lets through about 22% of contrast at periods of 6.3/11.9/23 px versus about 3.5% for the equal-variance Gaussian (roughly 6x less) - exactly text-stroke and letter scale. So the UI hint "What you see here is what lands in the file" (ShotViewer.tsx:1107) is false in the dangerous direction. Additionally the Rust doc comment (shot.rs:129-134) saying the preview "blurs the whole picture and clips afterwards" is likely inaccurate: Chromium's backdrop-filter samples only within the element (mirror edges), so near edges the two differ the other way.
fix: Approximate a Gaussian with 3 box passes per axis keeping the variance: `r_i = ((1.0 + 4.0*r*(r+1)/3.0).sqrt() - 1.0) / 2.0`, rounded and >= 1; run `blur_rows` 3x each way and widen the margin to `3*r_i` (still O(n)). Consider a minimum radius tied to the rectangle height (e.g. >= h/4) or pixelate-then-blur, and offer a solid "redact" fill. Fix the doc comment.

title: Save-path failures other than writeScreenshot are swallowed in ShotViewer
claim: The save catch is `catch { /* "The notice is already in the store." */ }`, which is true only for `writeScreenshot`. A throw in `layerBytes` (`getContext`/`toBlob` returning null) or in the follow-up `screenshotEdit` shows nothing.
fix: Set `lastError` in that catch for non-writeScreenshot failures.

title: Temp-file names collide across concurrent saves and leftovers are never cleaned up
claim: The main PNG temp is `target.with_extension(format!("{}.new.png", std::process::id()))` (commands.rs:633) and shot.json uses a fixed `shot.json.part` (shot.rs:353). Two concurrent saves of the same clip in one process write the same temp files, and nothing ever cleans up leftovers.
fix: Use uuid or atomic-counter suffixes plus a startup sweep of `*.new.png` and `*.part`. A per-clip lock (from ED-3) also fixes the collision.

title: Avoidable work on every save (base.png re-encode, ffmpeg spawn, Reset re-encode)
claim: On every save `base.png` is re-encoded even on marks-only saves where the crop is unchanged; an ffmpeg process is spawned per save for the thumbnail; and the Reset path re-encodes the original instead of copying it.
fix: Skip writing base.png if `read_edit(id).crop == crop && base exists`; build thumbnails in-process (see ED-11); copy the original on Reset.

title: Pen strokes copy the whole points array per sample and miss coalesced events
claim: Pen strokes copy the whole points array on every sample (O(n^2)) and don't use `getCoalescedEvents()`, so fast strokes come out angular. `bounds()` uses `Math.min(...xs)` spreads, which can hit V8's argument limit on extremely long strokes (speculative).
fix: Append points without copying, use `getCoalescedEvents()`, and compute bounds with a loop instead of spread.

title: Hooks called after an early return in ShotViewer
claim: `if (!clip) return null;` at ShotViewer.tsx:421 is followed by `useEffect` (453) and `useRef` (462). If `clip` ever went from defined to undefined React would throw "Rendered fewer hooks than expected". It can't happen today (Clips.tsx always passes `min(open, len-1)` with `len > 0`), so the early return is effectively dead, and rules-of-hooks lint fails.
fix: Move those hooks above the guard.

title: Watermark scale() degenerates when upscaling, producing a blocky mark unlike the smooth preview
claim: `scale()` in watermark.rs:179-205 assumes downscaling. For frames taller than about 2171 px (152/0.07, e.g. 5K, 8K or tall crops) it degenerates to nearest/box sampling, so the burned-in mark is blocky while the `` preview is smooth.
fix: Use bilinear sampling when `step < 1`.

title: ShotViewer.tsx is a 1650-line component holding too much state
claim: ShotViewer.tsx (about 1650 lines) holds the viewer, the load/save state machine, undo history, crop layer, side panel, Disclosure/PanelButton and `layerBytes`. Several bugs (ED-4, ED-5, ED-6) stem from that state being spread across closures.
fix: Extract `useShotEdit(id)` (load, save, race guards, busy, error), `useUndoHistory`, `CropLayer.tsx`, `AnnotatePanel.tsx`, and a `layers.ts` (render and encode).

title: Each editor mode decodes a different full-resolution PNG in the WebView
claim: View, draw and crop modes each use a different ground image (finished file, base.png, image.png), so every mode switch decodes a different full-res PNG in the WebView.
fix: No specific fix given.

title: OpenClipboard called with a NULL owner window (unsupported for SetClipboardData)
claim: The clipboard is opened with `OpenClipboard(HWND::default())`. MSDN says that with a NULL owner, `EmptyClipboard` sets the owner to NULL and `SetClipboardData` "fails". It works in practice, but it's unsupported.
fix: Pass the main window's HWND to OpenClipboard.

title: External edits to the screenshot are silently overwritten on the next ClippiBoy save
claim: `edit_screenshot` rebuilds from the stored original (`image.png`) every time (commands.rs:539) without checking whether the main file was changed externally; the DB dimensions also go stale.
fix: Record size and mtime (or a hash) of the last written file in shot.json; on mismatch warn, or adopt the external file as the new original.

title: Blocking sync commands marked #[tauri::command(async)] run on tokio workers
claim: `write_screenshot`, `copy_clip_image` and `take_screenshot` are sync fns with `#[tauri::command(async)]`, which (likely, per Tauri 2.11 macro behaviour) runs them on async runtime workers. They do blocking work there: PNG decode/encode, blur loops, `replace_file`'s sleep-retry (up to about 2.75 s), the blocking ffmpeg wait, and `Clipboard::open`'s sleeps.
fix: Make them `async fn` and wrap the body in `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`.

title: Sidecars committed before the main PNG; several screenshot writes are not atomic
claim: In edit_screenshot the write order is `shot.write_png(&base_path)` (`File::create` truncates base.png in place), then `write_edit(...)` (shot.json), then `write_picture` (temp + `replace_file`, retried 10x then fails with "Is it open somewhere right now?"). The comment at commands.rs:555 ("Everything that can fail happens before the first byte is written") is not true for these three writes. `keep_original` copies to `image.png` with a plain `std::fs::copy`, and `write_under` writes `under.png`/`under.json` non-atomically as well.
fix: Write all three to temp names first (`base.png.part`, `shot.json.part`, `<name>.<uuid>.new.png`). Then `replace_file` the main PNG (most likely to fail); only on success rename the sidecar parts (or remove base.png); on failure delete the parts. `keep_original`: copy to `image.png.part` and rename. `write_under`: same for under.png and under.json.

title: Save racing a file move or delete orphans the edited PNG and leaves the DB pointing at the unedited file
claim: `edit_screenshot` reads `clip.path` once at the start (commands.rs:518) and writes to it about 0.5-2 s later; nothing locks the clip. Closing the viewer runs `for (const id of seen) if (left.has(id)) void fileClip(id);` (Clips.tsx), and `file_clip` moves the file (favorites or game folder) and updates the DB path. The viewer's close button, Escape after Discard, and the footer Delete button all stay enabled while `busy`.
fix: Add a per-clip busy set in `AppState`: `write_screenshot` holds it; `file_clip` and `delete_clip` wait for it or skip. Re-read `lib.get(id).path` immediately before `replace_file`, inside the library lock. Disable Close and Delete while `busy`, or defer `fileClip` until the save resolves.

title: Editor usable before its edit store loads; failed load swallowed; save then drops crop/marks and misplaces blurs
claim: The load is `api.screenshotEdit(id).then(...).catch(() => {})` and tools are enabled with `disabled={!inTauri || broken}` with no check of `edit`. While `edit` is null: `full = clip.width` (the cropped size), `origin = {0,0}`, draw mode draws on `clip.path` (marks already baked in), and Save sends `write(edit?.crop ?? null, shapes)`, i.e. crop = null. If the load resolves late, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded))` silently wipes whatever was drawn in the meantime.
fix: Disable tools and Save until `edit !== null`; show the load error instead of swallowing it; have `write` refuse to run while `edit` is null.

title: Save's async continuation is not tied to the clip it started for; old edit lands on the next picture
claim: After `await writeScreenshot(...)` the code runs `const loaded = await api.screenshotEdit(clip.id); setEdit(loaded); resetShapes(readMarks(loaded));` using the closure's (old) `clip`, with no check that the viewer still shows it. Discard is always enabled (1089) and the step/navigation buttons are enabled once `mode === "view"` (1249, 1259).
fix: Keep `const shownId = useRef(id)` and bail out after each await when `shownId.current !== clip.id`. Better: have `write_screenshot` return the new `ShotEdit` directly.

title: Marks drawn while a save is running are silently discarded
claim: AnnotateLayer stays interactive while `busy` (ShotViewer.tsx:880-892). When the save finishes, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded)); … setMode("view")` (632-638) replaces everything drawn since Save was clicked.
fix: Block input while `busy` (`pointer-events: none` overlay or BusyVeil), or snapshot `current.current` at save time and re-apply any newer shapes as unsaved.

title: PNG decompression bomb in read_png/read_rgba (allocation before any size check), reachable via friend-shared screenshots
claim: `read_png` allocates the frame buffer from IHDR alone: `let mut buffer = vec![0u8; reader.output_buffer_size()];` (shot.rs:455-472); png 0.17's `Limits` only cap row and chunk buffers, not this caller-allocated buffer. `read_rgba` (shot.rs:676-689) checks the layer's dimensions against the picture only after the full allocation and decode (`blend`, shot.rs:105-108). Received shared files go straight into the library (share.rs:633-692).
fix: After `read_info`, reject anything with `w as u64 * h as u64 > 1<<28` (and dimensions > 16384), then allocate with `try_reserve_exact`. Give `read_rgba` the expected `(w, h)` and reject on mismatch before allocating. At receive time read the header and store the real dimensions.

title: Layer PNGs travel over IPC as JSON number arrays and are buffered by serde as Content
claim: `layerBytes` returns `Array.from(new Uint8Array(await blob.arrayBuffer()))`, so each byte becomes about 3.6 JSON characters plus a JS Number, stringified on the UI thread. On the Rust side `Step` is internally tagged (`#[serde(tag = "kind")] … Layer { png: Vec<u8> }`), so serde first buffers the whole object into `Content` (one ~32-byte `Content::U64` per PNG byte) and then copies into `Vec<u8>`.
fix: Send layers as raw IPC bodies (`invoke("write_shot_layer", bytes, { headers: { id, index } })`, Rust reads `tauri::ipc::Request` -> `InvokeBody::Raw`), or at minimum base64 strings with `#[serde(with = "...")]` and an adjacently/externally tagged enum. Encode in a worker with `OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob`.

title: Preview and save use full-resolution canvases per blur-separated run
claim: Preview canvases are `<canvas width={width} height={height}>` at full picture pixels (ShotAnnotate.tsx:566-586). Every blur splits the layer runs, so N blurs mean N+1 canvases of 3840x2160 (33 MB each; 132 MB each at 8K) plus the draft canvas. Save allocates another N full-size canvases at once (`Promise.all(... layerBytes ...)`, ShotViewer.tsx:609-618); at 8K this can fail, and `getContext`/`toBlob` returning null throws and is swallowed (see the swallowed-failures finding).
fix: Size preview canvases to `round(box.width*devicePixelRatio)` with `ctx.setTransform(scale…)`, repainting on zoom. Serialise `layerBytes` (or use OffscreenCanvas in a worker).

title: Arrow shaft's round cap pokes past the head's tip
claim: The arrow is a straight shaft with a filled triangular head of length `max(size*4, 10)` and round caps (ShotAnnotate.tsx:212-233). The shaft runs to the tip, so its round cap pokes out past the tip, blunting the point on thick arrows.
fix: Stop the shaft at the base of the head so the round cap doesn't poke past it.

title: Saving exits draw mode and clears undo history
claim: Undo history is cleared on every save (`resetShapes` at ShotViewer.tsx:267-272, called at 634), and saving exits draw mode (ShotViewer.tsx:638).
fix: Stay in draw mode after saving (638). Optionally keep undo across the save.

title: Zoom percentage is relative to fit; no 1:1 view or zoom keys
claim: The zoom % badge (ShotViewer.tsx:921-934, 932) shows zoom relative to the "fit" size, not actual pixels. There is no "1:1" view and no keyboard zoom keys.
fix: Ctrl+0 fit, Ctrl+1 actual pixels, Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- zoom (lockdown already cancels the browser's own handling).

title: No pan in draw mode without a middle button; wheel deltaX ignored
claim: The middle button pans in any mode but the left button pans only in view mode (ShotViewer.tsx:496-517, 502-503). The wheel only zooms (771-779) and horizontal scroll (`deltaX`) is ignored. There is no Space+drag. Touchpad users therefore cannot pan in draw mode.
fix: Make the wheel without Ctrl pan and Ctrl or pinch zoom, and add Space+drag.

title: Crop selection has corner handles only
claim: The crop selection can be drawn, moved or resized with 4 corner handles only (ShotViewer.tsx:1396-1405); there are no edge handles.
fix: Add edge handles (plus typed X/Y/W/H fields and pixel presets, see Better crop).

title: TS watermark rectangle is a hand copy of Rust with no parity test
claim: `lib/watermark.ts` `markRect` is a hand copy of Rust `watermark::rect_kept` (watermark.rs:94-125), linked only by a "change one, change both" comment (watermark.ts:6-8). A manual comparison found 0 mismatches today, but no test guards the parity.
fix: A Rust test writes or compares `fixtures/watermark_rects.json`, and vitest asserts `markRect` against the same file.

title: Handles and drawing surface are unfocusable, unlabelled divs
claim: The resize handles and the drawing surface are plain divs (lines 917-943 and 962-984; the report's table attributes 962-984 to ShotViewer.tsx, but the handle rendering via `handlesOf(chosen, measure).map(...)` is in ShotAnnotate.tsx). They cannot be focused and have no labels.
fix: Handles become focusable buttons with labels; keyboard creation of marks (Enter places a default-size mark at view centre, arrow keys move it).

title: Segmented control has no radiogroup or pressed semantics
claim: `Segmented` (Controls.tsx:47-89) has no radiogroup or pressed semantics, so assistive technology cannot tell which option (e.g. Outline/Filled/Both) is active.
fix: `Segmented` as `radiogroup` with `aria-checked`.

title: Colour swatch labels announce hex codes
claim: Swatch labels in ColorPicker.tsx read out hex codes (e.g. "Colour #ef4444") instead of colour names.
fix: Named swatches ("Red").

title: Escape with a mark selected goes straight to the discard question
claim: In the key handler, Escape leaves crop, then leaves draw mode (asking about unsaved marks), then closes the viewer (ShotViewer.tsx:379-386). With a mark selected it goes straight to "discard all marks?" (385) instead of deselecting first.
fix: Escape deselects first, then switches to Select, and only then leaves the editor.

title: "Save marks" enabled when nothing changed
claim: The "Save marks" button's disabled condition is only `shapes.length === 0` (ShotViewer.tsx:1065), so it is enabled with nothing changed and rebuilds and rewrites a 4K file for nothing.
fix: Disable "Save marks" when nothing changed.

title: "Crop" and "Undo crop" silently save unsaved marks
claim: "Crop" (ShotViewer.tsx:1150) and "Undo crop" (1174) also save any unsaved marks without saying so.
fix: Say so in the label ("Crop & keep marks") or ask; longer term unify crop and annotate into one session with one Save.

title: Text scale handle responds only to vertical distance
claim: Text has one scale handle, and scaling uses only the vertical distance (ShotAnnotate.tsx:818-828); horizontal pulls do nothing.
fix: No explicit fix proposed.

title: Clicking an existing caption with the Text tool creates a new one
claim: With the Text tool active, clicking an existing caption creates a new caption instead of editing the existing one (ShotAnnotate.tsx:741-744); editing requires double-click.
fix: No explicit fix proposed.

title: Picking a tool while cropping silently drops the crop selection
claim: `pickTool` (ShotViewer.tsx:585-592) switches to draw mode; when a crop selection is in progress it is silently dropped.
fix: No explicit fix proposed (unifying crop and annotate into one session addresses it).

title: Gallery tiles crop non-16:9 screenshots
claim: Gallery tiles are `aspect-video object-cover` (Clips.tsx:466, 483), so screenshots cropped to 1:1 or 9:16 look cut off in the gallery.
fix: No explicit fix proposed.

title: Screenshot tiles have no "edited" marker
claim: Screenshot tiles in the gallery (Clips.tsx:466, 483) show no marker indicating the screenshot has been edited.
fix: No explicit fix proposed.

title: Ellipse blur: antialiased preview vs hard-edged oval mask in file
claim: For an oval blur, the preview clips with an antialiased `border-radius:50%` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:1062), while Rust uses a hard in/out oval test (shot.rs:199-208). The preview's oval edge is smooth; the file's has a hard edge, so preview and file drift.
fix: Feather the Rust oval mask by coverage; add parity tests.

title: Pen marks cannot be resized
claim: `handlesOf` returns no handles for pen marks (ShotAnnotate.tsx:457), so a placed pen stroke can be moved but never resized.
fix: No explicit fix proposed beyond listing it as a gap.

title: Comments claim export is the preview canvas, but export is redrawn
claim: Comments at ShotAnnotate.tsx:166-172 and 607-610 say "the export is this very canvas". In fact the export is drawn again on a fresh full-resolution canvas (`layerBytes`, ShotViewer.tsx:1600-1606). Harmless but misleading for anyone extending the code.
fix: Update the stale comments.

title: IPC types are hand-copied between TypeScript and Rust
claim: `ShotStep`, `ShotEdit` and `ShotRect` are written by hand in both languages (types.ts:511-547, commands.rs:400-444), so they can drift silently.
fix: Generate the shared types with ts-rs or tauri-specta.

title: "Edited" pill counts unsaved marks
claim: The "Edited" pill (ShotViewer.tsx:532) counts unsaved marks rather than reflecting what is saved.
fix: Make the pill reflect the saved state.

title: Zoom resets on every mode change and save
claim: The zoom/pan view resets on every mode change and on every save (ShotViewer.tsx:372).
fix: No explicit fix proposed beyond listing it (stay in draw mode after saving).

title: Restyling a selected mark doesn't become the tool default
claim: When a mark is selected, the panel edits that mark's style via `restyle` (ShotViewer.tsx:651-687, 676-687) but does not write `styles[chosen.tool]`, so the tool's default for the next mark is unchanged and the next mark reverts (e.g. the next arrow is red again).
fix: When a mark is selected, `restyle` should also write `styles[chosen.tool]`. Persist styles in `localStorage` as `{color, altColor, sizeFactor: size/baseStroke(width), fill, outline, round}` and rebuild sizes per picture in `defaultStyles` (1488-1509), wrapping storage access in try/catch.

title: Copy picture is only reachable via right-click in view mode, not in the editor
claim: Copy picture (CF_DIB, read back from the edited file) and Copy file (CF_HDROP) exist only in the right-click menu, which is in the gallery and on the stage in view mode only (clipMenu.tsx:161-180, ShotViewer.tsx:767-770). There is nothing in the editor and no Ctrl+C.
fix: Add a "Copy" button in the footer and "Save & copy" next to "Save marks" (`write()` then `api.copyClipImage`); Ctrl+C copies the picture.

title: Watermark is re-stamped on edits even after the user turned it off
claim: Re-stamping the watermark during an edit depends on `under.png` existing, not on the current watermark setting (commands.rs:540-545, 585-587; watermark.rs:144-149). A user who has switched the watermark off still gets it re-stamped on older screenshots when editing them. The report calls this a product decision to make explicitly.
fix: Decide explicitly; `under.png` would make it easy to honour the current setting.

title: Marks are an opaque, doubly-encoded string the core cannot use
claim: In `shot.json`, `marks` is the `Shape[]` JSON encoded a second time as a string (shot.rs:311-320), and the core never reads it (316-318). So the core cannot validate marks, migrate them, render headlessly (presets or auto-redact at capture time), or export the current state; "Copy what I see" requires saving first.
fix: Sidecar v2 with `marks` as a real JSON array (`serde_json::Value`) and a reader that also accepts the old string.

title: Blur step coordinates are u32, so one negative value fails the whole save
claim: Blur step coordinates are `u32` on the Rust side, so a single negative number fails the whole save at deserialization. The TS side works around this by clamping drags (ShotAnnotate.tsx:770-775).
fix: Accept signed values and clamp in Rust.

title: Header close button discards unsaved marks without asking
claim: In ShotViewer, the header close button (the ✕ at ShotViewer.tsx:749-758) calls `close` directly, so it closes the viewer without the unsaved-marks check that the Escape path performs (ShotViewer.tsx:380-386, 580-583). This contradicts the comment at ShotViewer.tsx:184-188.
fix: Route the header ✕ through a `requestClose()` that does `if (editing && unsaved) setAskingDiscard(true) else close()`. Optionally keep a draft of `shapes` per clip id in `sessionStorage` so a crash or update restart can offer "Restore unsaved marks?".

title: Sidecar shot.json has no version and parse failures silently become "no edit"
claim: `shot.json` is `{crop: Rect|null, marks: string}` with no version field (shot.rs:311-320). Old marks are recognised only by missing fields, e.g. `outline !== false` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:192-194), with such rules scattered. `read_edit` turns any parse error into "no edit" via `unwrap_or_default` (shot.rs:335-340). If a newer version's file is opened by an older build, the editor would show `base.png` (cropped) as if it were uncropped and could wipe the edit on the next save.
fix: Sidecar v2: Rust `#[serde(default)] version: u32` (missing means 1) and `marks: serde_json::Value` with a reader that also accepts the old string; refuse to edit when `version > SUPPORTED`, returning `readOnly: true` instead of `unwrap_or_default`. TS `readMarks` accepts a string or array, then one `normalizeShape()` fills defaults. Migrate lazily on next save.

title: Shortcuts stop working after a slider or colour field gets focus
claim: The global key handler skips every INPUT element, including `type=range` (ShotViewer.tsx:378). So once the thickness slider or the hex/RGB colour field has focus, Delete, Ctrl+Z and Escape are ignored. The drawing surface calls `preventDefault` on pointerdown (ShotAnnotate.tsx:713-718, line 718), which stops it from taking focus, so drawing on the picture does not take focus back and the slider keeps focus indefinitely.
fix: Skip only text-entry fields (`input:not([type=range],[type=checkbox],[type=button])`, `textarea`, `[contenteditable]`). In `onDown`, blur `document.activeElement` when it is not the caption field.

title: "Remove all marks" saves immediately with no confirmation or undo
claim: The "Remove all marks" action (ShotViewer.tsx:1095-1104) writes the file at once without asking. Because undo history is reset on every save (`resetShapes` at ShotViewer.tsx:634), the marks are gone for good.
fix: Add a confirmation (reuse `ConfirmDelete`), or make it undoable by keeping the previous `marks` string.

title: Marks are invisible while cropping
claim: In crop mode the crop ground is the untouched original (ShotViewer.tsx:439-441), and the marks layer is only mounted in draw mode (ShotViewer.tsx:880-892). The user therefore cannot see their marks while choosing a crop, even though the crop cuts through them.
fix: Mount read-only `ShapeLayer`s and `BlurPatch`es in crop mode at the original's coordinates (`shift` by +origin).

title: Text font names Inter but Inter is not bundled
claim: Text marks use the font `600 {size}px Inter, "Segoe UI"` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:284-286), but Inter is not bundled (no `@font-face`), so in practice text renders as Segoe UI Semibold.
fix: No explicit fix proposed (the report notes it as a fact; option B mentions a bundled Inter).

title: Pacer never skips ticks and muxer discards PTS: encoder deficit or dropped frames become ever-growing A/V desync and eventually silent clips
claim: The frame pacer pace() in convert.rs:705-733 never skips ticks: `let due = start + period * index as u32; … if due > now { sleep } else if index > 0 { latest.overruns.fetch_add(1, …) } … index += 1; … let pts = (index as i64 - 1) * 10_000_000 / fps as i64;`. pts is derived purely from the tick index, so when the loop falls behind (encoder submit can block up to 500 ms via `send_timeout(job, SUBMIT_WAIT)` at mft.rs:1184) pts keep advancing 1/fps per frame regardless of wall-clock time. The muxer then throws packet PTS away and muxes the raw ES as CFR with `-f h264 -r fps` (muxer.rs:263), while audio is mapped via `qpc_of = base + pts_us*10` (pipeline.rs:535-537) and the snapshot sets `audio_frames = packets.len()*SR/fps` (pipeline.rs:1002-1003). A sustained encoder deficit or dropped frames therefore become ever-growing A/V desync and eventually silent clips. Overruns are only logged; nothing appears in the UI.
fix: When now − due > period, set index = elapsed/period (skip ticks) so pts stay true to the wall clock. Mux with real timestamps: a VFR container fed with packet PTS (a minimal NUT/MKV/TS writer piped to ffmpeg), or cut audio per packet at qpc_of(pts). Surface the overrun and drop rate in the UI.

title: Sleep/resume or a long thread stall makes the mixer allocate the whole gap in one window (OOM abort); pacer replays every missed tick
claim: The mixer thread sizes each window from the full elapsed gap with no cap: `let frames = ((target - from) * SAMPLE_RATE as i64 / 10_000_000) as usize; … shared.audio.mix_window(&sources, from, frames, &mut buffers);` (pipeline.rs:780-785), and AudioEngine::mix_window does `track.resize(sample_count, 0.0)` per source plus a scratch buffer of the same size (audio/engine.rs:346-350). After sleep/resume or any long thread stall the whole gap is allocated at once, which is an OOM abort. The pacer likewise replays every missed tick back-to-back. There is no WM_POWERBROADCAST handling anywhere.
fix: If target − from exceeds about 1 s, account the gap as ring silence and jump from. In the pacer, resync index when more than about 250 ms behind. Stop and restart the pipeline on PBT_APMSUSPEND / resume.

title: NV12 slot reuse is guarded by job count but slots rotate once per conversion, so frames queued for or held by the encoder get overwritten
claim: Latest::submit picks one of SLOTS = 22 NV12 textures round-robin on every WGC conversion: `let slot = self.next_slot; self.next_slot = (self.next_slot + 1) % self.slots.len();` (convert.rs:337-338). The reuse guard counts jobs rather than slots: `*depth as u64 + stats.in_flight.load(..) >= SLOTS as u64` (convert.rs:646, within 643-650; pacer submit path convert.rs:660-681). Because WGC converts on its own thread pool thread independently of the pacer, textures referenced by queued jobs (bounded(4) channel) or held in flight by the encoder can be overwritten with newer pictures, or written while NVENC/AMF reads them. MinUpdateInterval is set best-effort with `let _ = session.SetMinUpdateInterval(interval);` (wgc.rs:208) and the code itself notes it is missing before Windows 11. Off-by-one: the job the pacer holds inside send_timeout is never counted.
fix: Carry the slot index in Job; keep a per-slot refcount; release a slot when the MFT drops the sample (MFCreateTrackedSample + IMFTrackedSample::SetAllocator callback); the converter takes a free slot or skips the frame. Simpler alternative: in the WGC callback only CopyResource into one 'latest BGRA' texture and convert to NV12 in the pacer at tick time, giving one conversion per job and cutting VideoProcessor and watermark GPU work 2-4× at high refresh.

title: Clip save copies the whole clip (and each WAV) into one Vec, doubling RAM and risking OOM abort with large buffers
claim: muxer::build concatenates the entire clip into one in-memory buffer before writing the temp .h264: `let mut stream: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(snapshot.packets.iter().map(|p| p.data.len()).sum::<usize>() + …); … std::fs::write(&video_path, &stream)` (muxer.rs:131-141). write_wav (pipeline.rs:238-256) likewise builds the whole WAV in a Vec after window() has already allocated the samples. With the default ring budget of 1.5 × bitrate × seconds (config.rs:100-108) and a buffer slider up to 600 s, a full-length save doubles RAM use.
fix: Stream the header and packets through a BufWriter, or pipe straight into ffmpeg (-f h264 -i pipe:0; stdout/stderr draining already exists). Write WAV samples incrementally (VecDeque::as_slices). Size the budget against GlobalMemoryStatusEx.

title: Clip-save temp files are written to the system drive (%APPDATA%) even when clips go to another volume
claim: The save temp directory is `temp_dir: config::data_dir().join("temp")` (state.rs:856), so the temp .h264 and WAVs always go to %APPDATA% on C:, regardless of the clip output folder.
fix: Put temp files on the output volume (or stream saves into ffmpeg without temp files).

title: COM reference to the video-processor input view leaks on every frame
claim: In convert.rs:336-347, `let input = self.input_view(...)?;` returns a `view.clone()` (an extra COM reference), which is passed as `pInputSurface: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(Some(input)),` into the VideoProcessor stream and is never recovered with ManuallyDrop::into_inner / dropped after VideoProcessorBlt. One reference leaks per frame.
fix: Keep stream in a local and call ManuallyDrop::into_inner(stream.pInputSurface) after the Blt, or don't clone (transmute_copy a borrowed pointer).

title: Refresh-rate snapping produces 59 fps on 59.94 Hz panels
claim: The refresh rate comes from integer dmDisplayFrequency (capture.rs:155-158) and `choices.push(refresh)` adds it as an fps step (capture.rs:598-606), so fractional rates are truncated.
fix: Treat ±1 Hz around a standard step as that step, or read the rational refresh rate from QueryDisplayConfig.

title: Encoder thread polls instead of blocking
claim: The encoder loop uses `jobs.recv_timeout(2ms)` (mft.rs:1330), `sleep(1ms)` (mft.rs:1354), and a busy-polling drain loop (mft.rs:1406-1411) around GetEvent(NO_WAIT).
fix: A helper thread doing a blocking GetEvent(0) and forwarding into a crossbeam channel, then select! over events and jobs (or BeginGetEvent).

title: Encoder thread never initialises COM
claim: On the clippiboy-encoder thread (mft.rs:1115-1131), MFStartup, MFTEnumEx and ActivateObject run without CoInitializeEx. This only works because other threads (audio ensure_com, windows-rs CoIncrementMTAUsage) keep the implicit MTA alive.
fix: Call CoInitializeEx(MTA) at thread start.

title: Mixer timeline truncates per window, so long recordings drift
claim: pipeline.rs:818 is `next_100ns = Some(from + frames as i64 * 10_000_000 / SAMPLE_RATE as i64);`, which floors away 1/3 to 2/3 of a 100 ns tick per window.
fix: Keep an origin plus a u64 sample counter.

title: Pipeline stop order contradicts its own comment (capture dropped after encoder)
claim: The field comment (pipeline.rs:577-578) says the capture 'Has to drop before the encoder', but stop() (pipeline.rs:746-750) drops the encoder explicitly first and `_capture` only goes when the function returns.
fix: Take and drop the capture first.

title: release.yml never runs cargo test
claim: The release workflow release.yml never runs `cargo test`.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: add cargo test to the workflow).

title: 22 NV12 slots allocated up front waste VRAM (S4)
claim: All SLOTS = 22 NV12 textures are allocated up front: about 68 MB at 1080p, 122 MB at 1440p and 273 MB at 4K of VRAM, even with a near-zero queue.
fix: Not given explicitly here (see proposal: adaptive slot pool grown on demand using tracked samples).

title: Screenshot path creates a new D3D device per screenshot
claim: shot.rs:516 creates a new D3D device for every screenshot grab().
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: reuse a device).

title: mft::run is ~225 lines and duplicates event handling in the drain loop
claim: mft::run is about 225 lines long and duplicates the MFT event handling in the drain loop.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: factor out shared event handling).

title: muxer::run and run_reporting duplicate error formatting
claim: muxer::run and muxer::run_reporting duplicate the ffmpeg error formatting.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: share one formatter).

title: frames*SR/fps audio-length formula is duplicated
claim: The `frames*SR/fps` formula for audio length appears twice (pipeline.rs:1002 and recorder.rs:546).
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: one shared helper).

title: Vestigial EncodedPacket.track / duration_us fields and audio cases in buffer tests
claim: EncodedPacket.track and EncodedPacket.duration_us, and the audio cases in the buffer tests, are vestigial.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: remove them).

title: The last ~80 ms of every clip is silent
claim: The mixer runs `AUDIO_LAG_100NS = 80ms` behind QPC now (pipeline.rs:42), and Pipeline::snapshot (pipeline.rs:983-1026) doesn't wait for the mixer to catch up, so window() fills the clip tail with zeros (80 ms minus encoder latency).
fix: Wait up to ~100 ms for the mixer horizon to pass the clip end, or trim the trailing packets.

title: Mixed German and English user-facing error messages
claim: German and English user-facing errors are mixed and reach banners via `?`, e.g. "Encoder starten", "Paket abholen", "Taktgeber", "NV12-Textur fehlt".
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: unify error language).

title: convert.rs is #![cfg(windows)], so pure pacer and slot logic can't be tested
claim: convert.rs is `#![cfg(windows)]`, so the pure pacer and slot logic inside it cannot be unit-tested (on non-Windows CI).
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: move pure logic out of the cfg(windows) module and test it).

title: B-frames with raw Annex-B remux at -r, pts-filtered snapshot and discarded PTS is fragile (S5)
claim: B-frames (enabled via CLIPPIBOY_BFRAMES or a driver default) combined with raw Annex-B remux at -r fps, a pts-filtered snapshot and discarded PTS is fragile.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report.

title: Screenshot read_back runs for every arriving frame, not just the first
claim: shot.rs:531-533 is `let _ = sender.try_send(read_back(&gpu, frame.texture));`, so the staging copy, a blocking Map and a 24 MB (4K) conversion run for every frame that arrives before the capture is dropped, even though only the first result can be sent.
fix: Check whether the channel is already full before calling read_back.

title: Async MF_E_TRANSFORM_STREAM_CHANGE handling consumes the HaveOutput event without retrying and never re-reads SPS/PPS
claim: On MF_E_TRANSFORM_STREAM_CHANGE (mft.rs:1015-1023) the code sets the new output type then does `return Ok(None)`, consuming the METransformHaveOutput event without calling ProcessOutput again. The SPS/PPS header is never re-read afterwards because catch_up_on_header (mft.rs:896-911) stops at the first non-empty header.
fix: Call ProcessOutput again immediately; re-read the header; as a fallback extract SPS/PPS (NAL 7/8) from the first IDR packet.

title: MinUpdateInterval equal to the frame period may skip alternate frames (S1)
claim: WGC MinUpdateInterval is set exactly equal to the frame period; because of jitter this may cause WGC to skip alternate frames.
fix: Since the pacer does CFR anyway, use about 0.5-0.9 × the period.

title: MFTEnumEx called without adapter LUID; MFT may belong to a different adapter (S2)
claim: MFTEnumEx is called without an adapter LUID, so on same-vendor multi-GPU machines the chosen MFT may belong to a different adapter than the D3D11 device.
fix: Use MFTEnum2 with the device's adapter LUID.

title: fps choices up to panel refresh exceed H.264 Level 5.2 at 1440p/4K (S3)
claim: The fps choices go up to the panel's refresh (165/240). At 1440p/4K that exceeds H.264 Level 5.2 (1440p ≤ ~144 fps, 4K ≤ ~64 fps).
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: cap fps per resolution/level).

title: No device-removed / encoder-death detection or recovery; errors only logged and a stale ring is saved as current
claim: Encoder failures are only logged: mft.rs:1312 and mft.rs:1344 are both `Err(err) => log::warn!("{err}")`; mft.rs:1174-1176 is `Disconnected => log::warn!("encoder has stopped — one frame is lost"); return false;`; the encoder thread exits quietly on event-queue errors (mft.rs:1284-1290). Nothing calls GetDeviceRemovedReason, and only `dropped` is counted (pipeline.rs:605-609). Shared::report() is only called on the capture path and only the first error per run is surfaced, so no banner appears and no restart happens.
fix: Send encoder/D3D errors through Shared::report. Add a status-tick watchdog: no new packet for more than 2 s, or GetDeviceRemovedReason() != S_OK, reports and auto-restarts with a new device. Treat D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET the same way, and flag saves whose newest packet is stale.

title: Recorder job queue is an unbounded std mpsc channel
claim: The recorder taps packets and audio blocks to its writer thread over `let (tx, rx) = channel::<Job>();` (recorder.rs:146), an unbounded std mpsc channel with no backpressure or fail policy.
fix: Use a byte-bounded channel with an explicit fail-and-stop policy.

title: Recorder file I/O runs while holding the packet-ring and tracks locks
claim: pipeline.rs:954 takes `let ring = self.shared.packets.lock();` and Recorder::start (create_dir_all, File::create, meta write + rename, thread spawn) runs at pipeline.rs:964 while that lock is held. open_track (recorder.rs:306-322) writes meta.json from the mixer thread while holding shared.tracks.
fix: Do the file creation before taking the lock and only install the recorder under it. Move the meta writes into the writer thread.

title: Recording free-space guard ignores mix.pcm and stems, so finalize fails on long multi-source recordings
claim: The room guard is `if free < needed + RECORDING_SPARE_BYTES` with `needed = estimated mp4 size` (lib.rs:894-895). It does not account for finalize's sum_tracks writing mix.pcm (recorder.rs:580-583) or per-track stems.
fix: Count mix PCM and stems in the guard, or skip pre-summing and let ffmpeg amix all the PCMs.

title: VideoProcessor auto-processing is not disabled, so driver enhancements may alter footage
claim: The VideoProcessor setup (convert.rs:141-168) only sets colour spaces; there is no `VideoProcessorSetStreamAutoProcessingMode(.., FALSE)`. Auto-processing is on by default.
fix: Disable auto-processing with VideoProcessorSetStreamAutoProcessingMode(.., FALSE).

title: VideoProcessor content description uses output size and sets no rects, so a resized window is stretched
claim: The content description in convert.rs:141-168 uses `InputWidth: width, InputHeight: height`, i.e. the output size rather than the source size, and no stream source/destination rectangle or background colour is set. The WGC frame pool is recreated on size change (wgc.rs:229-242) but window capture does not restart (state.rs:774).
fix: Set stream source and destination rects that preserve aspect (letterbox) with a black background, and use the real source size in the content description.

title: ffmpeg/ffprobe runs have no timeout and no kill-on-close job object
claim: muxer::run uses `command.output()` (muxer.rs:65-68); run_reporting (muxer.rs:432-458) does `.stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::piped()).spawn()` then `child.wait()`; ffprobe (muxer.rs:476-488) uses `.output()`. None has a timeout/kill, and children are not placed in a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.
fix: Put ffmpeg/ffprobe in a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; wait with a timeout and kill.

title: ffmpeg inherits the parent's stdin (no Stdio::null, no -nostdin)
claim: run_reporting (muxer.rs:432-458) spawns ffmpeg with piped stdout/stderr but no stdin setting and without `-nostdin`, so stdin is inherited.
fix: Use Stdio::null() for stdin plus -nostdin.

title: Orphaned .part.mp4 files in the clip folder are never cleaned up
claim: The in-progress output `<stem>_<id>.part.mp4` is written beside the target clip (muxer.rs:323), but the startup leftover cleanup (lib.rs:677-688) only cleans data_dir/temp.
fix: Sweep stale *.part.mp4 at startup.

title: Closed or recreated window is never recovered during window capture
claim: The WGC Closed handler only sets a flag and reports once (pipeline.rs:689-695). Drift detection returns None for windows: `|| config.target_kind != TargetKind::Monitor` (state.rs:772-776), so nothing restarts or re-targets capture.
fix: Stop the buffer, or re-resolve the window by process and restart.

title: halt_pipeline holds the pipeline mutex during the stop
claim: state.rs:559-561 is `if let Some(mut pipeline) = self.pipeline.lock().take() { pipeline.stop(); }`; under Rust 2021 the temporary lock guard lives across stop().
fix: Bind the take() result to a local first.

title: Hardware MFT is never shut down (no IMFShutdown / ShutdownObject / SET_D3D_MANAGER(0))
claim: The MFT is created by `candidates[pick].activate.ActivateObject()` (mft.rs:716) and the IMFActivate is dropped at the end of build. The run ends with only `ProcessMessage(MFT_MESSAGE_NOTIFY_END_STREAMING, 0)` (mft.rs:1440-1444). There is no IMFShutdown::Shutdown, no IMFActivate::ShutdownObject, and no MFT_MESSAGE_SET_D3D_MANAGER(0). Media Foundation makes the caller of ActivateObject responsible for shutdown, and async MFTs own event queues and worker threads.
fix: Store the activate object. After the drain: SET_D3D_MANAGER(0), then cast::<IMFShutdown>()?.Shutdown(), then activate.ShutdownObject(). Send MFT_MESSAGE_NOTIFY_END_OF_STREAM before COMMAND_DRAIN.

title: Replay ring length and byte limits are not enforced when only one keyframe exists
claim: Trimming in the ReplayBuffer only runs `while self.keyframes.len() > 1 {` (buffer.rs:93), and the no-keyframe safety net returns early with `if !self.keyframes.is_empty() || self.packets.is_empty() { return; }` (buffer.rs:128). With exactly one keyframe neither the pts-length nor the byte-budget limit applies and the safety net is skipped, so the ring grows without bound. The GOP read-back from the encoder is only logged. Existing tests only cover zero or many keyframes.
fix: If no keyframe arrives within 2× GOP, force one (CODECAPI_AVEncVideoForceKeyFrame). When over budget with a single GOP, drop the ring and wait for the next IDR (memory should win, as the module's own doc says). Add a unit test for the single-keyframe case.

title: sum_tracks duplicates write_mix_wav
claim: recorder::sum_tracks duplicates the mixing logic of write_mix_wav.
fix: Not given explicitly in the report (implied: share one implementation).

title: A launcher's leftovers tap also records the game, so game audio is in the clip twice
claim: In `Leftovers::assign` (audio/mod.rs:201-207) the coverage check `let covered = spoken_for.contains(&root) || ancestors(root, tree).iter().any(|parent| spoken_for.contains(parent));` only asks whether a leftovers root sits *below* something already recorded, never whether it sits *above* it. In addition, `SourceKind::Game => taken.extend(game_pid),` (mod.rs:289) excludes only the game pid itself, not `app_root(game_pid)`. Launchers (Steam, Battle.net, Epic, Riot Client) start the game as their child, and the repo's own test fixture notes steam.exe "holds sessions on every device". So steam.exe becomes a leftovers root and is tapped with `INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE`, which includes its child, the game. Same class: if the game's parent runs the same exe (a launcher stub), the leftovers tap that parent and record the game again.
fix: In `assign`, also skip any root that is an ancestor of a taken pid: `taken.iter().any(|t| ancestors(*t, tree).contains(&root))`. For such a root, tap its other session-holding descendants one by one instead (accept that the launcher's own sound is lost, or surface a warning). Use `app_root` for the game in both `taken` and the tap. Add a test with steam.exe as the parent of game.exe.

title: Clips with one audio track: gain compounds on every save, and mute permanently strips the audio
claim: When a clip has no individual tracks (only one WAV at save time, e.g. "desktop audio only", or a legacy clip), `from_stems == false` and the audio comes from `format!("0:a:{}", track.index)` of input 0. When nothing is cut at the front, input 0 is the current clip file (`VideoSource::Clip`), which already has the previous gain baked in. The editor (ClipEditor.tsx:113-121) still shows a gain/mute row for that single track and `apply_clip_edit` stores the mix, so every later save re-applies it on top and adds one more AAC generation. A front cut instead reads the original, so the level jumps back. Muting the track makes `mix_filter` return `None`, which yields `-an`; without an original the audio is gone for good, `clip_tracks` then returns 0 tracks, so `dirty` (ClipPlayer.tsx:535) can never become true and Save is disabled for that clip forever. With an original present, later saves fail because `0:a:0` no longer exists in the target.
fix: For single-track clips, always take the audio from `edit::source_path(clip)`, seeked to `stems_start_ms`, so it stays one generation from the original and the gain is relative to it. Alternatively, write a stem (a copy of the original track) on the first edit. Or hide/disable gain and mute when `!separate`, and store neutral values after baking them in.

title: Endpoint loopback on 5.1/7.1 devices drops the centre and surround channels (game dialogue)
claim: The packet conversion in capture.rs:280-287 keeps only the first two channels: `if src_channels == 1 { left = sample; right = sample; } else if channel == 0 { left = sample; } else if channel == 1 { right = sample; }`. There is no downmix of centre/LFE/surround channels. Device mode (endpoint loopback) is what "Quick setup" creates (default output device + mic; AudioMixer.tsx:506-511).
fix: Either initialise the device client with `float_format()` and `AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY` so Windows does the downmix and resampling, or implement an ITU downmix driven by `dwChannelMask`.

title: In device mode (Quick-setup default), ClippiBoy's own sounds and the editor preview are recorded into the buffer
claim: Excluding ClippiBoy's own pid only happens in leftovers mode; plain endpoint loopback (capture.rs:334-336) records everything rendered on the device, including sounds played by sounds.rs:55-58.
fix: One of: when there is a single output source, use process loopback in `EXCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE` mode on ClippiBoy's own pid; or at least warn about it in device mode; or play the chimes on another endpoint (`eCommunications`).

title: Export-to-size truncates the duration to whole seconds and overshoots the target
claim: `export::recipe` computes `let seconds = (target.duration_ms / 1000).max(1);` (export.rs:79), which truncates the duration, so the bitrate budget is computed for a shorter clip than the real one.
fix: Compute in ms: `video_bits * 1000 / duration_ms / 1000`.

title: Export resolution loop always downscales sources taller than 1080p (and 900p to 720p) even with ample budget
claim: The resolution step-down loop in export.rs:83-93 sets `height = step` *before* checking the budget, so any source taller than 1080 (1440p, 4K, 1200p) is always scaled to <=1080p, and 900p to 720p. This contradicts the comment "anything taller than the first is left where it is", and no test covers 1440p.
fix: First check whether the source height itself fits the budget before stepping down; add a test for 1440p.

title: Rolling back the first cut can delete the only copy of the recording
claim: In the swap-in rollback (edit.rs:559-568): `if let Err(err) = replace_file(temp, target) { if first_cut { let _ = move_across(&archive, target); let _ = std::fs::remove_file(note_path(&clip.id)); let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir(&clip.id)); } let _ = std::fs::remove_file(temp);`. At this point the target has already been renamed into the originals store. The result of `move_across` is ignored, so if the move back fails, `remove_dir_all` deletes the archive and `temp` is deleted as well. This contradicts the doc comment "the clip can never disappear entirely".
fix: Delete the note and folder only when `move_across` returned `Ok`. Otherwise leave note + archive in place so `repair` arm 1 (`(false, Some(_), true)`) restores it on the next start, and keep `temp` too.

title: First cut across drives: a crash during the copy makes `repair` mark the untouched clip as trimmed
claim: `move_across` (edit.rs:497-511) uses `std::fs::copy(from, to)` straight onto `video.mp4` in the originals store. When clips are on D: and AppData on C: (the case the README describes), copying several GB takes seconds to minutes. If the app is killed during the copy, on restart target, note and a partial `video.mp4` all exist and the DB row has no `original`, which matches repair arm `(true, Some(note), true) if clip.original.is_none()` ("swapped, but the database never got its turn", edit.rs:945-948), so `set_original(note)` runs; `settle` returns early because the clip's size is unchanged. Related: if the copy fails partway, swap_in (edit.rs:550-556) removes temp and note but leaves the partial `video.mp4`, and `source_path` (edit.rs:87-94) checks only that `video.mp4` exists, so it hands the partial file to later `clip_tracks` and edits until the next restart.
fix: Copy to `video.mp4.part`, fsync, then rename within AppData; delete `.part` files in `repair`. In arm 3, check that the clip really is trimmed (probed length < `note.duration_ms` - tolerance) before trusting the note. Better: keep the originals store on the same volume as the clip (e.g. a hidden `.clippiboy/originals` folder) so the move is always an atomic rename, which also removes copying GBs to C: without checking free space.

title: The activation completion handler can signal a closed event handle after a timeout
claim: On a 5 s activation timeout (capture.rs:177-192) `CloseHandle(event)` runs while the async operation still holds the completion handler (capture.rs:389-393), which holds the raw HANDLE; a late `ActivateCompleted` then calls `SetEvent` on a closed handle, which may since have been reused for another event (unsafe). Also, `Error::from_win32()` after `WAIT_TIMEOUT` reports GetLastError = 0 ("The operation completed successfully").
fix: Let the handler own the event (close it in `Drop`) and return an explicit timeout HRESULT.

title: Log spam: `live_pid` logs every 2 s, twice per pass
claim: `live_pid` (mod.rs:139-141) logs "'{exe}' is {now} now" whenever the live pid differs from the stored one, but the stored pid is never updated, so once an application has restarted every `resolve` (every 2 s, twice per pass) logs it again.
fix: Log only when the value changes, or write the new pid back to the config.

title: No limiter on the summed mix
claim: The main-mix WAV is summed with i16 `saturating_add` (pipeline.rs:225-234) and the edit re-mix uses `amix … normalize=0` (stems.rs:349-352), with no limiter on either.
fix: Add an `alimiter`/true-peak limiter (-1 dBTP) on `[aout]`, and optionally a soft clipper in `write_mix_wav`.

title: Leftovers mode spawns a thread and loopback client for every idle application holding a session
claim: In leftovers mode, every idle application that holds an audio session gets its own capture thread and process-loopback client.
fix: No explicit fix given in the report.

title: `default_output_id` and `list_devices` enumerate every endpoint and its property store every 2 s
claim: `default_output_id` and `list_devices` enumerate every audio endpoint and open its property store on every 2 s pass.
fix: No explicit fix given; related: follow device changes via `IMMNotificationClient` instead of polling.

title: `AppState::new` applies audio config synchronously on the main thread at startup
claim: At startup, `AppState::new` calls `apply` synchronously on the main thread (state.rs:308), which can block up to 5 s per slow stream.
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: apply the audio configuration off the main thread.

title: No free-space check before copying the original on a first cut
claim: On a first cut, the original is copied into the originals store without checking free space first.
fix: No explicit fix given; related: keep the originals store on the same volume as the clips.

title: `convert` allocates a stereo Vec on every capture packet
claim: `convert` allocates a `stereo` Vec on every packet in the realtime capture path (capture.rs:251).
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: reuse a per-stream buffer.

title: `mix_window` allocates `scratch` on every 10 ms tick despite its doc comment
claim: `mix_window` allocates `scratch` on every 10 ms tick (engine.rs:355), despite the doc comment "rather than allocating".
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: keep and reuse the scratch buffer.

title: AudioContext leaks if `createMediaElementSource` throws
claim: In `useClipMix.ts`, an AudioContext created inside the `try` block is not closed if `createMediaElementSource` throws.
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: close the context in the error path.

title: Leftover German strings in log and test messages
claim: Some log and test messages are still in German, e.g. "blieb liegen", "Pegel", "bildgenau…".
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: translate the strings to English.

title: `export_for_discord` reuses stale or half-written files and never fixes an oversize one
claim: `export_for_discord` (commands.rs:871-888) decides reuse with `let ready = std::fs::metadata(&output).map(|meta| meta.len() > 0 && meta.len() <= target_bytes)`: there is no freshness check against the source clip. `shrink` writes straight to the final file name, so a crash/kill leaves a truncated MP4 without moov that counts as "ready" from then on. Two quick presses run two ffmpeg processes with `-y` on the same file. An over-limit result is put on the clipboard regardless, and the next press re-encodes the same recipe and gets the same overshoot.
fix: Check `stems::is_newer(&output, &source)`; write to `*.part`, then rename; allow one export per clip at a time; retry at a lower bitrate when the file is over the limit.

title: UI `audible` treats soloed+muted as audible, unlike the core
claim: The UI's `audible` in useClipMix.ts:19-21 is `anySolo ? state.solo : !state.muted`, which treats a soloed and muted track as audible, unlike the core rule (`enabled && !muted && (!any_solo || solo)`). The comment claims the two are the same.
fix: No separate fix given in the report; implied: make the UI's `audible` match the core rule (muted always wins).

title: Applications running elevated are stored as "PID n" and can never be found again
claim: The process name lookup in devices.rs:91-96 uses `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ)` plus `GetModuleBaseNameW`, which fails for elevated processes. The UI then stores `exe: "PID 1234"`.
fix: Take the name from the `process_tree()` snapshot, or use `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`, which needs only limited query rights.

title: Meter peak uses load-then-store instead of `fetch_max`
claim: The meter peak update in ring.rs:130-133 uses an atomic load followed by a store instead of `fetch_max`, so concurrent updates can lose a higher peak.
fix: Use `fetch_max`.

title: `plan` can produce a 200 ms excerpt starting at the very end of the file
claim: For very short trims, `edit::plan` can produce a 200 ms excerpt starting at the very end of the file, because the end is clamped past the duration.
fix: No explicit fix given in the report.

title: Autoplay-blocked AudioContext leaves preview silent and the error is swallowed
claim: In `useClipMix.ts`, `ctx.state !== "running"` returns early, so an AudioContext blocked by autoplay stays silent while the video is muted, and `play().catch(() => undefined)` hides that failure.
fix: No explicit fix given in the report.

title: Export target computed in MiB while Discord may enforce decimal MB
claim: The export target size is computed in MiB. If Discord enforces decimal MB, "10 MB" exports land 4.9% over the limit.
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: compute the target in decimal MB.

title: Export starvation check assumes 30 fps
claim: The starvation check uses `bitrate_for(.., 30)` (export.rs:89), assuming 30 fps regardless of the clip's real frame rate, so the check is 2x too optimistic for 60 fps clips.
fix: Use the real fps; consider stepping to 30 fps before dropping resolution.

title: One-pass ABR/CBR export leaves only a 3% size margin
claim: Export-to-size uses one-pass ABR/CBR with only a 3% margin, and the result is not verified against the target size.
fix: Use x264 two-pass, or verify the result and re-encode with `bitrate × target/written × 0.97` when it is over.

title: The resampler is stateless and per packet, with no anti-aliasing
claim: The linear resampler in capture.rs:298-312 restarts the phase at 0 on each packet, and `next` is clamped inside the packet, so the last samples are held instead of interpolated into the next packet. `target_frames = (frames as f64 * ratio) as usize` truncates, dropping up to one frame per packet, which the ring's slew then has to absorb. There is no anti-aliasing filter.
fix: Use the AUTOCONVERTPCM + SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY flags (as for the multichannel downmix issue), or a stateful resampler (`rubato`) kept per stream.

title: A single bad timestamp inserts silence and then shifts the source late for tens of seconds
claim: In `SampleRing` (ring.rs:151-163) any block whose stamp is over 50 ms late is treated as a real gap and immediately filled with zeros; the correctly stamped blocks that follow show negative drift, which may only slew at 2000 ppm (50 ms takes about 25 s). Negative drift between -50 ms and -1 s is never treated as a discontinuity. In capture.rs:631-657, `AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_TIMESTAMP_ERROR` (0x4) is ignored (only SILENT 0x2 is handled), and for devices on the fallback clock the read-time `now` is used as the stamp.
fix: Detect real gaps with `pu64DevicePosition` (pass it instead of `None`), which jumps by exactly the missing frames; ignore stamps flagged 0x4; with the fallback clock use `now − (GetCurrentPadding + frames)/rate`; require two agreeing blocks before filling a gap and re-anchor on a sustained negative drift; add tests for these cases.

title: No MMCSS, and the 80 ms mixer lag discards late packets
claim: Capture threads (capture.rs:470-499) and the mixer thread run at normal priority with no `AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW` (MMCSS). The mixer reads with an 80 ms lag (`AUDIO_LAG`, pipeline.rs:42); a packet that lands in the ring after the mixer has already pushed zeros for that window is lost from the clip.
fix: Register the threads with MMCSS ("Audio"/"Capture"); raise `AUDIO_LAG` to about 200-250 ms (a replay buffer does not need low latency; the save can wait for the mixer to pass the last frame's QPC).

title: `snapshot()` hands over live TrackRings with only 2 s slack; front of clip audio may scroll out before being read
claim: `snapshot()` hands over the *live* `TrackRing`s, which keep only 2 s of slack, and the WAVs are only written after the whole h264 file has been written. The audio windows are not copied inside `snapshot()`.
fix: Copy the windows inside `snapshot()`.

title: Sources set to "the default device" do not follow default-device changes
claim: There is no `IMMNotificationClient` (grep-confirmed). An empty `device_id` (capture.rs:320-327) binds to whatever was the default at stream start and stays there until that device becomes invalid. The fingerprint `out:` never changes, so the stream is never restarted. The configuration warning even claims the source "follows the Windows default device".
fix: Register `OnDefaultDeviceChanged` and restart the affected stream.

title: Leftovers catch-all rule never matches a source configured as the default device ("")
claim: In `Leftovers::assign` (mod.rs:235) the catch-all rule compares `*device == self.default_device`; for a source configured as "the default device" `device` is `""` while `default_device` is the real endpoint id, so the catch-all never matches such a source.
fix: Normalise `""` to the resolved default device id before assigning.

title: Drawing the waveform holds the whole decoded audio in RAM; no per-clip lock; muted clips re-run ffmpeg
claim: The waveform uses ffmpeg's `showwavespic` (preview.rs:49-53), which queues every input frame until EOF (s16 mono), about 345 MB per hour of recording. There is no lock, so StrictMode/double opens write the same PNG concurrently; a long waveform job also keeps the clip open. Fully muted clips (no audio stream) re-run ffmpeg and error on every open.
fix: Put `aresample=8000`/`asetnsamples` before `showwavespic`, or compute min/max peaks in Rust from `-ac 1 -ar 4000 -f s16le pipe:1`; add a per-clip lock.

title: Preview sync tolerates up to 120 ms offset and corrects with audible hard seeks
claim: In `useClipMix.ts`, tracks are only corrected when off by more than 120 ms (line 317), with a hard seek once a second (line 353). An A/V offset of up to 120 ms persists, and each correction is an audible skip.
fix: Use a threshold of about 30-40 ms and nudge `playbackRate` by ±1-3% for small corrections, seeking only above about 150 ms. Or decode the tracks into AudioBuffers and schedule them against `ctx.currentTime`.

title: Preview silence watchdog trips on genuine silence or buffering and permanently switches route
claim: The silence watchdog in useClipMix.ts:238-252 trips on two seconds of genuine digital silence (AAC of zeros decodes to exact zeros) or on elements still buffering, and then permanently switches to the attenuate-only route.
fix: Switch only if no sample was non-zero since the graph was built.

title: An application picked by a child pid (Discord) records only that child; the other session is recorded nowhere
claim: In `audio::resolve`, `taken` excludes `app_root(live_pid)` (the whole Discord process tree) from the leftovers (mod.rs:292-298), but the application stream taps `pid: now`, the live pid itself (mod.rs:336-345). `list_processes` returns *session* pids, and for Discord those are its utility children (the repo's own `discord()` fixture); the UI stores one of them (AudioMixer.tsx:787-795).
fix: Tap `app_root(live_pid)` in `resolve`, consistent with `taken`. Also deduplicate the process picker by root.

title: A capture-start timeout leaves a zombie capture thread and WASAPI client running forever
claim: On the start timeout (capture.rs:127-136) the code returns `Err(_) => Err("timed out starting the audio source".into()),` without setting `stop`, and the JoinHandle is dropped. If the device's `Activate`/`Initialize` answers after 5 s, the thread sends into a dead channel and then pumps into an unreferenced ring forever, holding the WASAPI client. `retry_failed` runs every 10 s and can pile these threads up.
fix: Call `stop.store(true, Relaxed)` before returning the timeout error; the thread checks it after init and exits.

title: Solo counts disabled sources and is persisted: a disabled soloed source silences every track
claim: The audibility rule in audio/mod.rs:448-451 is `let any_solo = sources.iter().any(|s| s.solo); source.enabled && !source.muted && (!any_solo || source.solo)`. `any_solo` also counts disabled sources, and solo is stored in the config, so the state survives restarts. Solo is destructive (affects what is recorded, not just monitoring).
fix: Use `sources.iter().any(|s| s.enabled && s.solo)`. Clear solo on disable and/or on startup. Add a configuration warning "solo active — N tracks record silence".

title: Level meters ignore solo and keep moving while the buffer records zeros
claim: `levels()` (audio/engine.rs:242) checks only `muted`, not `audible()`, so a source silenced by another source's solo still shows live meter levels.
fix: Make the meters follow `audible()`.

title: Preview elements recreated after the fallback route never get the current `playbackRate`
claim: In `useClipMix.ts`, `<audio>` elements recreated after falling back to the old route never receive the current `playbackRate` until the next `ratechange` event.
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: apply the current `playbackRate` when creating the elements.

title: Colour metadata (VUI) is not carried over on re-encode
claim: When a first cut re-encodes, `-colorspace`/`-color_primaries`/`-color_trc` are not set, so the colour metadata (VUI) of the source is not carried over.
fix: No explicit fix given; implied: pass the source's colour metadata via `-colorspace/-color_primaries/-color_trc`.

title: No recovery when the clip database cannot be opened; new clips are never indexed
claim: If `Library::open` fails (state.rs:274-280), the library stays `None`. Saves still write files but are never indexed (lib.rs:123-127), and there is no rescan.
fix: Run an integrity check, rename the corrupt file aside, and rebuild by scanning the clip folder.

title: `Library::delete` reports success while the file stays on disk
claim: `Library::delete` ignores a `remove_file` error, then deletes the row anyway (clips.rs:315-330).
fix: Fail or retry the file removal before deleting the row.

title: Case-sensitive path comparisons in filing cause spurious `x (2).mp4` renames
claim: Path comparisons in filing are case-sensitive (filing.rs:101, :121), although Windows paths are case-insensitive.
fix: Not stated in the report (implied: compare paths case-insensitively on Windows).

title: Control token never rotates; another local user can squat the port and harvest it
claim: The control token never changes across runs.
fix: Rotate the token each run.

title: Log file has no size limit within a run
claim: logging.rs:59-63 rotates the log only at start; there is no size limit within a run.
fix: Add a size cap or daily rotation.

title: Unparseable friends-server messages are logged in full (presence data, friend IDs)
claim: friends.rs:521 logs the *entire* server message when parsing fails, which can include presence data and friend IDs.
fix: Truncate or redact unknown messages before logging.

title: No Unicode normalization of game folder names
claim: Game folder names (filing.rs:41-72) are not Unicode-normalized.
fix: Not stated in the report (implied: Unicode-normalize game names before deriving folder names).

title: Control port is on by default and lets any web page detect ClippiBoy
claim: The control port is enabled by default on every install, even without a Stream Deck, on a fixed port (127.0.0.1:47653).
fix: Keep the control port off until the Stream Deck plugin is detected.

title: Control port does not check the Host header; Origin/Referer/Sec-Fetch-Site heuristic has DNS-rebinding gaps
claim: The control server does not check the Host header. Its browser defense relies on refusing requests carrying Origin, Referer or Sec-Fetch-Site, which has gaps: a same-origin GET sent with `no-referrer` carries none of them. Today the token is the real protection.
fix: Require `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`.

title: Dead asset-protocol scope entry `$APPDATA/ClippiBoy/**`
claim: The asset scope entry `$APPDATA/ClippiBoy/**` in tauri.conf.json resolves to `%APPDATA%\gg.clippiboy.app\ClippiBoy`, which does not exist (tauri path/desktop.rs:247), so the entry is dead. Do not "fix" it to `$DATA`, which would expose config.json and friends.json.
fix: Not stated explicitly (implied: remove the dead entry); do not change it to `$DATA`.

title: `msSmartScreenProtection` disabled in WebView2 browser args
claim: `additionalBrowserArgs` in tauri.conf.json disables `msSmartScreenProtection`. Informational, because only local content is loaded.
fix: None required (informational).

title: `export_for_discord` size computation `megabytes * 1024 * 1024` is unchecked
claim: `export_for_discord` computes `megabytes * 1024 * 1024` unchecked (commands.rs:872).
fix: Use `checked_mul` and clamp.

title: `save_clip(Some(seconds))` bypasses the normal save flow
claim: `save_clip(Some(seconds))` (commands.rs:375-382) skips `begin_save`, tagging, the `clip-saved` event and the banner. The UI never sends `Some`.
fix: Remove the `Some` path or route it through `save_clip_and_notify`.

title: Stringly-typed command errors: repeated `.map_err(|e| e.to_string())` and "clip not found"
claim: commands.rs uses `type Result<T> = Result<T, String>`, with 39 `.map_err(|e| e.to_string())` and 21 `"clip not found"` occurrences. `thiserror` is already a dependency.
fix: Introduce a serializable `CmdError` enum using `thiserror`.

title: Repeated clip lookup logic in commands.rs; no `clip_by_id` helper
claim: Commands repeat the same look-up-clip-or-"clip not found" pattern instead of using a shared helper.
fix: Add a `clip_by_id(&state, &id)` helper.

title: Three `*_and_notify` functions duplicate the same post-save sequence
claim: The three `*_and_notify` functions in lib.rs:105-271 repeat the same index, tag, emit, notify, sound, telemetry and banner sequence.
fix: Extract an `announce_saved` function.

title: `spawn_ui_updates` is a 160-line loop driven by magic `tick %` values
claim: `spawn_ui_updates` (lib.rs:928-1089) is a 160-line loop whose jobs are scheduled by magic `tick %` values.
fix: Use per-cadence scheduled jobs.

title: Mixed German and English in comments, logs and capability descriptions
claim: Comments, logs and capability descriptions mix German and English: lib.rs:853-857, :931-958, commands.rs:762 "blieb liegen", `.clippiboy-schreibtest`, and default.json "Rechte des Hauptfensters".
fix: Not stated in the report (implied: use one language consistently).

title: Uninstall leaves session token, control token, database, large caches and autostart entry behind
claim: There is no uninstall hook in hooks.nsh. Tauri's "delete app data" removes `%APPDATA%\gg.clippiboy.app` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gg.clippiboy.app`, but the real data is in `%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy` and survives: friends.json (session bearer token), the control token, clips.db, gigabytes of originals and tracks, logs. The HKCU Run autostart value also stays. All of this is in the *Roaming* profile.
fix: Add `NSIS_HOOK_POSTUNINSTALL` behind the same checkbox, remove the autostart entry, and move the large stores to LocalAppData.

title: Missing tests for delete_clip(""), mock-config saves, folder-name edge cases and oversized control-port requests
