claim: There are no tests for: `delete_clip("")`; a mock config reaching `set_config`; reserved names and case handling in `folder_name`; and the control port's handling of oversized requests.
fix: Add tests for these four cases.

title: `path UNIQUE` with `INSERT OR REPLACE` silently deletes another clip's row and tags
claim: The clips table declares `path UNIQUE` (clips.rs:38) and inserts use `INSERT OR REPLACE` (clips.rs:100). Latent row loss.
fix: Not stated in the report (implied: avoid INSERT OR REPLACE deleting other clips' rows on a path conflict).

title: Game folder name sanitizer misses some Windows reserved device names
claim: The reserved-name list in the game folder-name sanitizer (filing.rs:41-72) misses `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, `COM¹-³`/`LPT¹-³`, and a name like `NUL .x` with a space before the dot.
fix: Not stated in the report (implied: extend the reserved-name handling to these names/patterns).

title: `clipboard::read_text` can read past the end of the clipboard block
claim: clipboard.rs:163-175 reads up to 4,000,000 UTF-16 units from the `CF_UNICODETEXT` global block until it finds a null terminator, without checking `GlobalSize`.
fix: Bound the read with `GlobalSize(block) / 2`.

title: Configured port 0 makes the handoff file name port 0 instead of the bound port
claim: Port 0 can be configured for the control server; the handoff file (`%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\streamdeck.json`) then names port 0 instead of the actually bound port.
fix: Write the actual bound port to the handoff file.

title: Asset scope `$VIDEO/**` exposes the whole Videos folder
claim: The asset protocol scope in tauri.conf.json includes `$VIDEO/**`, exposing the entire Videos folder, while `$VIDEO/ClippiBoy/**` is enough.
fix: Narrow the scope to `$VIDEO/ClippiBoy/**`.

title: Unused opener and global-shortcut plugin permissions granted
claim: The capabilities grant `opener:default`, `opener:allow-reveal-item-in-dir` and `global-shortcut:default`, but the frontend imports no opener or global-shortcut module and does not use them.
fix: Remove these permissions.

title: CSP lacks `base-uri`, `form-action` and `object-src` restrictions
claim: The CSP in tauri.conf.json does not set `base-uri`, `form-action` or `object-src` (script-src falls back to 'self', and `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is acceptable).
fix: Add `base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; object-src 'none'`.

title: Deep-link match is loose: `clippiboy://authX` is accepted
claim: The deep-link handler matches with `strip_prefix("clippiboy://auth")`, which also matches `clippiboy://authX` and similar.
fix: Parse with `url::Url` and require host `auth`.

title: Startup failure `.expect("could not start ClippiBoy")` aborts without telling the user
claim: lib.rs:1367 uses `.expect("could not start ClippiBoy")`, which aborts without any user-visible message.
fix: Show a native message box before exiting.

title: Local process can crash ClippiBoy or hang its UI through the control port without the token (tiny_http body drain)
claim: The control port (control.rs, tiny_http 0.12.0, bound to 127.0.0.1:47653, on by default) answers requests that fail the token/header check with a 403 on its single serving thread: control.rs:156-158 `if !allowed { return respond(request, 403, …) }`, with `respond` at control.rs:325-336. In tiny_http 0.12.0, request.rs:191-216 wraps any body larger than 1024 bytes in `EqualReader`, and `util/equal_reader.rs` has a `Drop` that does `let mut buf = vec![0; remaining_to_read];` and then blocks reading the rest of the body from the socket. No socket timeouts are set anywhere, and `util/task_pool.rs` creates one thread per connection with `thread::spawn` with no upper limit. So dropping the request allocates and reads whatever body size the client *declared* (Content-Length), before and regardless of the token check. `control::stop()` (control.rs:94-106) waits on `thread.join()` forever; it is called from `set_config` (commands.rs:154-158) when the port or on/off changes and from `regenerate_control_token` (commands.rs:1384), both sync commands on the main thread.
fix: Replace tiny_http with a small server you control (std `TcpListener`, or tokio which is already a dependency) with a read timeout of about 2 s, at most 8 KB of headers, rejection of `Content-Length` above 4 KB before building the request, closing the socket rather than draining it, and a cap of about 8 connections; or patch tiny_http. Separately make `stop()` not block forever: join with a timeout, or detach.

title: Startup tidying in `setup()` runs on the main thread before the window paints
claim: `setup()` (lib.rs:1189-1230) runs `edit::repair`, `thumbs::migrate`, `normalize_games`, `filing::tidy` (renames with sleeps) and `discard_leftovers` on the main thread before the window paints. The code comments themselves mention about 3 s.
fix: Do the setup tidying on a background thread.

title: `Library::get` reads the whole library (and does filesystem checks per clip) to find one clip
claim: clips.rs:186-188 is `Ok(self.list()?.into_iter().find(|c| c.id == id))`. `list()` reads every row and every tag, and for each clip calls `edit::has_original`, which costs 2-3 `is_file` checks (clips.rs:145, edit.rs:73-79, :97). Almost every command calls `get` one to three times, under the library mutex, mostly on the main thread.
fix: Query with `WHERE id = ?1` plus the tags for that one id, and compute `original_available` only for the clip being returned.

title: config.json writes can race and corrupt the file; a corrupt file silently resets to defaults
claim: `replace_config` writes to disk *outside* the config lock (state.rs:368-402), while `control::ensure_token` and `regenerate_token`, `repair_screens` and `hide_to_tray` write *inside* it (control.rs:124, :364; lib.rs:505, :1139). Both paths write the same `config.json.tmp` (config.rs:181-183), with no fsync. On a parse failure `load()` quietly falls back to defaults (config.rs:167-170). The comment at config.rs:244-248 itself calls this "the most expensive bug this file can have".
fix: One write lock around snapshot-and-write, a unique temp file name, `sync_all()` before rename, and keep `config.json.bad` plus a last-known-good copy on a parse failure.

title: Capabilities give false least privilege: every window can call all 79 app commands (no app ACL manifest)
claim: build.rs is plain `tauri_build::build()`: there is no `AppManifest`, and gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json has no `__app__` entry. Tauri 2.11.5 webview/mod.rs:1823 checks the ACL only `if (plugin_command.is_some() || has_app_acl_manifest || !is_local)`, so capabilities gate only plugin commands and every window (main, overlay, console) can call all 79 app commands. overlay.json describes itself as "only listens, controls nothing", yet the overlay can call `delete_clip`, `set_config`, `clipboard_read_text`, `export_clip`, `friends_delete_account` and so on.
fix: Use `tauri_build::Attributes::new().app_manifest(AppManifest::new().commands(&[...]))` and grant commands per window. The overlay needs roughly nothing; the console needs only its clip and friends subset.

title: `export_clip` writes to any renderer-supplied output path (overwrite, UNC NTLM leak, ffmpeg http upload)
claim: `export_clip` (commands.rs:1155-1169) takes `output: String` straight from the UI. `shrink` (commands.rs:1094-1097) only refuses `output == source`. ffmpeg then runs with `-y` (export.rs:124) and the output as its last argument, with no restriction to local file paths or protocols. Part of the finding that a compromised renderer gets user-level read and write on the whole filesystem (defense in depth).
fix: Show the save dialog from Rust and keep the chosen path server-side, or at least require an absolute local drive path: no `\\`, no `scheme:`, an allowed extension. Add `-protocol_whitelist file` to export, trim and thumbnail ffmpeg calls.

title: `set_clip_dir` / `set_config` accept any clip folder and grant it recursively to the asset protocol
claim: `set_clip_dir` (commands.rs:266-290) and `set_config` (commands.rs:54-98) accept any directory, and `allow_clip_dir` grants it *recursively* to the asset protocol (lib.rs:1095). `set_config` does not validate `clip_dir` at all. Speculative: with an empty `clip_dir`, Tauri builds the pattern `\**` (scope/fs.rs:489-498), which may match every canonicalized path.
fix: Show the folder dialog from Rust and keep the chosen path server-side; canonicalize and validate `clip_dir` in `set_config`; refuse empty, system or profile-root folders.

title: `reveal_path` accepts any path, UNC included
claim: `reveal_path(path)` (commands.rs:1347) accepts any path from the renderer, UNC paths included, with no check that it lies inside the app's known folders. Part of the finding that a compromised renderer gets user-level filesystem access (defense in depth).
fix: Make `reveal_path` accept only paths inside the known folders.

title: `delete_clip` with an empty or colliding id wipes every clip's audio tracks and untouched originals
claim: commands.rs:680-683 runs `stems::remove(&id); edit::remove(&id); crate::thumbs::remove(&id);` *before* checking the clip exists. `muxer::sanitize` (muxer.rs:470) maps "" to "", so `stems::dir("")` is `tracks\` and `remove_dir_all` deletes the whole store (stems.rs:44-46, :146-148). `edit::remove("")` does `remove_dir_all(originals\)` (edit.rs:61-63, :114-118), which holds every trimmed clip's only untouched copy and every screenshot original. The library delete is then a no-op and the call returns `Ok`. Because `sanitize` maps `-` to `_`, passing another clip's UUID with underscores destroys that clip's stores. The side-file deletion also happens before the database commit, so a failed `lib.delete` still loses the side files.
fix: Look up the clip first and return `Err` if it is missing. Take the store paths from `clip.id` as stored. Make `sanitize` return an error for empty or non-UUID input. Commit the row delete before removing files.

title: `set_config` runs heavy work on the main thread, including MFTEnumEx on every change
claim: Sync `#[tauri::command]` functions run on the event-loop thread; while one runs the UI does not paint, and `window_awake` in the UI-update thread waits on the main thread, stalling the 2 s tick too. `set_config` is sync: `replace_config` calls `encode::resolve`, then `list_encoders`, then `mft::available_encoders()`, which runs MFTEnumEx on *every* change, including slider drags (state.rs:367). It also writes the config, refreshes audio and reads the registry for autostart. On a capture-source change it calls `stop_pipeline` plus `start_buffer_and_notify` (commands.rs:117-121); stopping waits for a save in progress, which takes seconds. `control::restart` waits on the server thread (see LS-1).
fix: Mark the command `#[tauri::command(async)]` or use `spawn_blocking`; cache the encoder list.

title: `file_clip` sleeps in rename retries on the main thread while holding the library lock
claim: `file_clip` (a sync command, main thread) calls `filing::move_file`, which retries `rename` with sleeps of 40 to 200 ms, about 0.6 s in total (filing.rs:269-285). It does this *while holding the library lock* (commands.rs:747), and the retries happen exactly when the player holds the file.
fix: Mark the command `#[tauri::command(async)]` or use `spawn_blocking`.

title: Debug-formatted iroh errors in logs can leak peer IP addresses
claim: share.rs:694 and :747 log Debug-formatted (`{:?}`) iroh errors, which can include peer IP addresses.
fix: Keep Debug detail out of info-level logs.

title: Share links publish the friend's name on received clips
claim: Received clips are tagged `tags: vec![format!("from {from}")]` (share.rs:866). `is_friend_tag` only matches a "with " prefix, so when the user shares a received clip as a public link, the tag "from <friend's Discord display name>" goes to the public page; the server-side `cleanTags` keeps it. This contradicts the stated intent ("who played along stays among friends, a link is public"; commit f041a3d).
fix: Treat "from …" as a friend tag, or better, store friend and sender tags in a structured field.

title: Session token stored in plaintext in Roaming AppData
claim: `std::fs::write(&path, json!({ "token": token }))` writes the bearer session token to `%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\friends.json` in plaintext. The token stays valid for 180 days without use (renewed with use), so it follows roaming profiles and backups and any same-user malware can take it. (No token appears in the logs.)
fix: Protect it with DPAPI (`CryptProtectData`) or the Windows Credential Manager (keyring), and keep it in LocalAppData.

title: Any clippiboy://auth deep link consumes the pending sign-in verifier
claim: `friends.verifier.lock().take()` runs before the `/auth/exchange` call, for any `clippiboy://auth?code=<junk>`. A web page (or local process) can therefore make a pending sign-in fail, and can pop error toasts when no sign-in is open. Login CSRF (victim signed into attacker's account) is blocked by PKCE unless the attacker also learns the victim's challenge (it travels in the URL query, so browser history or server logs) within 10 minutes — that part is speculative.
fix: Keep the verifier until an exchange succeeds or a timeout passes; ignore links silently when no sign-in is in progress.

title: P2P exposes IP addresses before accept, and friend-chosen endpoints/relays get dialled
claim: The offer contains `router.endpoint().addr()`: the sender's public and LAN IPs, sent to the friend before they accept. On accept, the receiver contacts IP:ports and a relay URL chosen by the friend (iroh's `start_active_relay` ignores whether the URL is in the relay map). That reveals the receiver's IP to an attacker-run relay and sends QUIC packets to arbitrary hosts, LAN included. The privacy page doesn't say that a friend learns your public and LAN IPs (the sender's as soon as it offers), or that a friend-chosen relay host may be contacted.
fix: Say this in the privacy page; offer only global addresses plus the n0 relay; ignore relay URLs outside the default map; consider a relay-only option.

title: Share temp tracks and crash .part files leak
claim: The cut tracks in `%TEMP%\clippiboy-share\<id>\` are deleted only after a successful send (`o.tracks.drain(..)`). After Declined, Expired, Cancelled or Failed they stay forever, and nothing cleans them at startup. `.part` files from a crash stay in the user's clip folder or under `tracks\`.
fix: `impl Drop` for `Outgoing` (or clean up on every end state), plus a startup sweep of those folders.

title: safe_file_name misses Windows device names and bidi control characters
claim: `safe_file_name` doesn't apply the reserved-name rules `filing::folder_name` has, so `CON.mp4` / `NUL.mp4.part` are possible: on Windows <= 10 the transfer fails or writes into a device. `COM¹`-style names aren't handled by either function. It doesn't strip Unicode format characters (`c.is_control()` misses U+202E), so a name can be shown as "…4pm.png" in Explorer, though it stays a `.mp4`.
fix: Reuse the reserved-name logic and strip the Cf bidi characters.

title: ffmpeg archive isn't hashed as a whole and nothing caps its size
claim: The ffmpeg zip download has no size cap, and `ZipArchive` parses the unverified file; entries are copied to disk before their hash is known (only per-file SHA-256 hashes are pinned). A compromised release could fill `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (a zip bomb or an endless stream). Nothing gets executed, though.
fix: Pin the zip's own SHA-256 and check it before opening; cap each entry at its expected size.

title: Reconnect backoff has no jitter
claim: The friends reconnect backoff has no jitter, so all clients come back together after a server deploy (thundering herd).
fix: Add random jitter to the reconnect backoff.

title: Privacy page says connection details of both devices pass the server; only the sender's do
claim: The privacy page says "connection details of both devices" pass the server; in fact only the sender's do (in the offer). The receiver's go directly to the friend. (The page's "never reaches our server" claim is also only true while the server behaves — see NW-1.)
fix: Correct the privacy page wording.

title: Two concurrent receives with the same file name share one .part file; duplicate offer ids can be accepted twice
claim: `free_name` only checks the final name, so two concurrent transfers both get `X.mp4.part`. The second takes its resume offset from the first one's partly written file and truncates it (`set_len`). Rust opens files with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so after the first renames the file into place, the second keeps writing into the clip that was already verified and filed. `rename` also replaces anything that appeared at the target since, and `free_name` hands back the existing target after 999 name collisions. An offer re-sent with the same id overwrites an entry that is already Moving and puts it back to Asking, so it can be accepted twice.
fix: Use a unique part name (`.<uuid>.part`); claim the final name atomically (`create_new`, or a move without replace, retrying on collision); reject duplicate offer ids.

title: P2P fetch/serve stalls never time out; router JoinSet unbounded; outgoing secret stays valid forever
claim: iroh sends a keep-alive every 5 s, so the QUIC idle timeout never fires while the peer process lives. In `fetch`, `open_bi`, `read_exact(header)` and `recv.read`, and in `serve`, `accept_bi`, `read_exact(length)` and `send.write_all` can therefore hang forever if the other side goes quiet. Cancel is only checked between chunks, so it cannot break a blocked call. The router's `JoinSet` is unbounded, so anyone who knows the NodeId can pile up idle connections. An outgoing transfer stays "Moving" with a working secret for good if the receiver disappears.
fix: Per-operation `tokio::time::timeout` (e.g. 30 s without progress); an expiry on outgoing secrets.

title: Friends WebSocket connect has no timeout, freezing the reconnect loop
claim: `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async` is called with no timeout; a middlebox that stalls the TLS handshake freezes the friends reconnect loop until restart.
fix: A 15 s timeout on the WebSocket connect.

title: Updater builder has no timeout, so one hung check stops all hourly checks
claim: The updater builder is constructed without `.timeout()`, so a single hung update check blocks and stops all subsequent hourly checks.
fix: Set a timeout on the updater builder.

title: Server-supplied link.id goes into URL paths unchecked
claim: `link.id` from the server goes into URL paths unchecked. A malicious server returning `../me` turns the take-down into `DELETE /me`. That only matters for the server operator, who controls the account anyway.
fix: Validate/escape `link.id` before building URL paths.

title: "Appear offline" still sends game and status to the server, not stated on the privacy page
claim: With "Appear offline", the app still sends game and status to the server (kept in memory and on the socket, not passed to friends). Consistent with "friends see you as offline", but not stated on the privacy page.
fix: State this on the privacy page.

title: Updater downgrade through the unsigned version field in latest.json
claim: The plugin's `release.version > self.current_version` comes from `latest.json`, which is unsigned; the minisign signature covers only the installer bytes. Someone with write access to the GitHub release (but without the signing key) can label an old, signed, vulnerable installer as 99.0 and it installs silently in passive mode. Nothing in the app's own code skips verification; this is a known limitation of the Tauri updater.
fix: After download, check that the signature's trusted comment (`file:ClippiBoy_<ver>…`) matches `update.version`, or keep a minimum-version floor in the app.

title: Any Discord user can re-request friendship right after being declined, triggering an in-game banner each time
claim: Any Discord user who knows a username can re-send a friend request immediately after being declined (index.ts `sendRequest`), and each request causes an in-game banner on the victim's side (friends.rs:360-366).
fix: Rate-limit or suppress re-requests after a decline.

title: handle_relay doesn't check that `from` is a current friend
claim: `handle_relay` doesn't check that `from` is in the current friend list; it relies entirely on the server for the friendship check.
fix: Check `from` against the local friend list in `handle_relay`.

title: Unverified whether Windows toasts escape friend-supplied text in XML
claim: Whether Windows toasts escape their XML (tauri-winrt-notification 0.7.3, not available locally) is unverified. The toast text comes from friends (display name, game, offer title) but only reaches a toast when banners are off.
fix: Verify that tauri-winrt-notification escapes text, or escape it before passing.

title: P2P handshake fully trusts the server: an active server can fetch or swap any clip
claim: The share offer relayed through the friends server carries everything needed to download: `Signal::ShareOffer { id, size, sha256, secret, addr, meta }`. The sender lets in anyone holding the secret, before any answer: `let open = matches!(entry.transfer.stage, Stage::Asking | Stage::Moving); if !same(entry.secret…) || !open` (comment: "Dialling in is their yes"). It never checks `connection.remote_id()`. iroh keys are new every run (`Endpoint::bind(presets::N0)`), so nothing can be pinned. The server sees every relay body (secret, sha256, sender address), so it can download or MITM the transfer. This breaks the privacy page's "never reaches our server" / end-to-end claim against anything other than a passive server.
fix: Keep a persistent iroh secret key per install, protected with DPAPI. The receiver puts its NodeId in `ShareAnswer`; the sender serves only after an accepting answer and only to that `remote_id()`. Pin each friend's NodeId on first use and warn when it changes; optionally show a short safety code. Reword the privacy page.

title: Size overflow in the offer lets a friend show "1.0 MB" and fill the disk; no size cap or free-space check on receive
claim: `let total = size + meta.tracks.iter().map(|track| track.size).sum::<u64>();` — the release profile has no `overflow-checks`, so this wraps. With `size` = 1 MiB and `tracks[0].size` = 2^64-1 the banner shows "1.0 MB". After accept, `fetch_tracks` asks for track 0, the sender answers `rest` = 2^64-1, which passes the `offset + rest != size` check, and the receiver writes `…\tracks\<id>\0.m4a.part` until C: is full. Even without the overflow trick there is no upper limit on size and no free-space check anywhere in `receive`, unlike the 2 GB guard recordings have.
fix: Use `checked_add` throughout. Reject offers above a sane cap (e.g. clip <= 64 GiB, each track <= 2 GiB, `track.size` <= `size`). Check free space on both volumes with `disk.rs` before accepting and while writing. Never write past `size`.

title: An accepted friend can spam offers: banner, sound and toast each time, plus a slow UI
claim: Every incoming offer inserts a map entry (an existing id is silently overwritten), plays `ClipReceived`, shows an overlay banner over the game and raises `Alert::Clip`, which is always wanted. The default is `accept_clips: AcceptClips::All`. The server's rate budget (30 messages per 10 s) is per WebSocket and is lost when the Durable Object hibernates, and a user may open any number of sockets, so the rate is effectively unbounded. Each `emit()` sends the whole transfer list to three webviews, so cost grows roughly with the square of the number of live offers (entries stay about 60 s or more).
fix: Client side: at most 1-2 pending offers per friend and about 10 in total; reject ids that are already known (incoming or outgoing); one banner and one sound per friend per 30 s. Server side: a persisted per-user budget and a cap on sockets per user.

title: An incomplete ffmpeg folder blocks setup for good, re-downloads every 30 minutes, and silently falls back to PATH ffmpeg
claim: Setup does `if PROGRAMS.iter().all(|(name, _)| target.join(name).is_file()) { return Ok(()) }`, otherwise it downloads, then `std::fs::rename(&staging, target)`. If `9.0.1\` exists but `ffmpeg.exe` is gone (antivirus quarantine is a common false positive, or the user deleted it), the rename onto the existing non-empty folder fails on Windows with "could not put ffmpeg in place". It retries every 30 minutes forever, pulling the full archive each time. Meanwhile `tool()` quietly falls back to `PathBuf::from("ffmpeg")` (app folder or PATH), an untested and possibly old ffmpeg that then also parses friends' files.
fix: When the folder is incomplete, `remove_dir_all(target)` before the rename (or unpack under a fresh name); don't fall back to PATH silently; keep the 30-minute retry from becoming a download loop.

title: Files from friends go to ffmpeg unchecked, with format auto-detection, no whitelists, no timeout, on an async worker
claim: The thumbnail for a received clip is made with `ffmpeg -ss 0.5 -i <received file> …`, and `file_clip` runs it synchronously inside the tokio task. Unlike the share-link server (`Mp4Boxes`), the P2P path never checks that the file is an MP4; ffmpeg picks the demuxer from the content. The pinned build's HLS demuxer refuses an `.mp4` name and concat runs with `safe=1`, which limits the obvious tricks, but ffmpeg parser bugs, playlist-style demuxers (DASH, concat reading sibling files) and any old PATH ffmpeg (NW-4) remain. `muxer::run` has no timeout/kill.
fix: For received files add input options `-format_whitelist mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2,matroska,webm,image2,png_pipe,jpeg_pipe -protocol_whitelist file` (and to every later ffmpeg/ffprobe input of such files), or check the box structure as the server does. Put a timeout and kill on `muxer::run`. Run `file_clip` in `spawn_blocking`.

title: Failed shrink leaves temp link file behind
claim: In share-link creation, a failed shrink returns early via `??` and leaves `temp\link-<id>.mp4` behind.
fix: Clean up on every end state (e.g. a Drop guard), plus a startup sweep of temp folders.

title: Friends outbox is an unbounded channel
claim: The friends outbox is an unbounded channel, so queued outgoing messages can grow without limit.
fix: Use a bounded channel.

title: .expect("HTTP client") in three client builders can abort the app
claim: `.expect("HTTP client")` is used in three HTTP client builders; if TLS setup ever failed it would abort the whole app, ending any recording in progress.
fix: Handle the builder error instead of panicking.

title: current_game MutexGuard held across overlay::show, which blocks on the main thread: possible permanent deadlock
claim: At lib.rs:216-221 `overlay::show(app, BannerKind::Recording, "Recording", state.current_game.lock().clone());` and at lib.rs:356 `Some(match state.current_game.lock().as_ref() { … })` the MutexGuard is a temporary in a call argument (or a `match` scrutinee), so it lives until the end of the statement, which includes the whole of `overlay::show`. Inside `overlay::show`, `window.is_visible()` (overlay.rs:404) and `window.hwnd()` (overlay.rs:479) are blocking main-thread round trips when called from a worker thread (tauri-runtime-wry's `getter!` sends a message to the main thread and waits on `rx.recv()`). These main-thread paths lock `current_game`: `engine_status` (sync command, commands.rs:316) -> `status_snapshot` (state.rs:736); the toggle-buffer hotkey (runs on the main thread) -> `start_pipeline` (state.rs:472/515); `set_config` -> `start_buffer_and_notify`. The worker holds `current_game` while waiting on the main thread, and the main thread waits on `current_game`, so the app deadlocks. Report: rare but a permanent hang; the pattern is confirmed, the interleaving is plausible.
fix: Read the value into a local first (`let game = state.current_game.lock().clone(); overlay::show(…, game)`) at both sites. Make it a rule that no AppState guard is alive while calling window APIs. Better still, send banners through a channel to one overlay worker thread.

title: Toggle-buffer hotkey starts and stops the capture stack on the UI (main) thread
claim: Global-shortcut Pressed handlers run on the main thread (inside the hidden hotkey window's window procedure). lib.rs:813-816: `if event.state() == ShortcutState::Pressed { toggle_buffer_and_notify(app); }` runs the toggle directly, while every other hotkey spawns a thread. The work done there: `launch_pipeline` spawns `ffmpeg -version` every time, because at state.rs:486 `!muxer::available() && tools::is_ready()` evaluates the expensive check first; `Pipeline::start` waits up to 10 s for encoder readiness (mft.rs:1135, `recv_timeout(10s)`); `lifecycle` may be held elsewhere, e.g. by `attach_recorder`'s 5 s keyframe loop (state.rs:1014-1020) or a `close_recording` whose writer is flushing to a slow disk; stop drains the encoder with unbounded joins. The comment at lib.rs:786 ("the hotkey arrives on one of its own") is wrong. Latent: the plugin's `unregister_all` holds its `shortcuts` lock while it waits on the main thread, and the hotkey handler takes the same lock on the main thread, so calling `register_hotkeys` off the main thread would deadlock (today only sync commands and `setup` call it, so it is not reachable yet).
fix: `std::thread::spawn(move || toggle_buffer_and_notify(&app))`, and swap the operand order at state.rs:486. Keep `register_hotkeys` on the main thread.

title: Persistent start failure makes the automation retry every 2 s with an error sound and banner
claim: state.rs:188-190: `if !buffer_active && !self.suppressed.load(SeqCst) { self.started.store(true, SeqCst); return AutoAction::Start; }`. `poll_always` (state.rs:246-252) has the same shape. Nothing records a start failure. Each failure runs `notify(error)`, `sounds::play(Error)` and `overlay::show(Error, "Buffer will not start")` (lib.rs:363-366). Error banners stay at least 6 s, so with a 2 s retry the banner never goes away. Each attempt also builds and tears down D3D, WGC, MFT and the ffmpeg probe during gameplay.
fix: Keep a failure count with exponential backoff. After N failures, set `suppressed` and announce it once.

title: Banner can get the wrong size or land partly off-screen on monitors with different scaling
claim: overlay.rs:532-533 calls `set_size(PhysicalSize)` and then `set_position`. Crossing to a monitor with another scale triggers WM_DPICHANGED, and tao rescales the window (allow_resize is true for non-maximized windows; checked in tao source), altering the size just set. The console works around this by placing twice; the overlay does not.
fix: Position, then size, then position again.

title: Overlay appears in Alt+Tab and Task View while visible (the whole recording with the REC badge on)
claim: tao implements `skip_taskbar` with `ITaskbarList::DeleteTab` only. The overlay window is not `focusable(false)` and has no WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW or WS_EX_NOACTIVATE, so it is listed in Alt+Tab and Task View whenever it is visible, which is the whole recording when the REC badge is on.
fix: `.focusable(false)`, or add WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW|WS_EX_NOACTIVATE.

title: Free space of 0 means both "unknown" and "disk completely full"
claim: lib.rs:860: `disk::free_bytes(...).unwrap_or(0)`, and `guard_recording_room` returns early when it reads 0 (lib.rs:890-893). A failed free-space query and a completely full disk are indistinguishable, and the room guard is off exactly at 0.
fix: A separate "known" flag, or `u64::MAX` as the sentinel.

title: A user override in games.json may or may not win, at random
claim: game.rs:198-206: `map.extend(extra)` runs before keys are lowercased. A user key `"CS2.exe"` and the built-in `"cs2.exe"` then collide in `.collect()`, and HashMap iteration order picks the winner.
fix: Lowercase the user's keys before `extend`.

title: Title-derived game name is overwritten on every tick
claim: state.rs:671 `(Some(_), _) => *held = name.clone()` overwrites a title-derived game name on every tick. Titles that change ("Loading", map names) fragment clip folders and spam presence updates.
fix: Pin the name per PID.

title: set_config replaces the whole config from the page's copy, reverting repair_screens corrections
claim: `set_config` replaces the whole config object with the page's copy. A stale settings page reverts `repair_screens`' monitor corrections, because `keep_once_flags` only covers two flags.
fix: Send patch-style updates from the UI.

title: Tray buffer CheckMenuItem stays checked after a failed start
claim: The tray's CheckMenuItem is toggled automatically by the menu library when clicked. After a failed start it stays checked, because `refresh` only calls `set_checked` when `buffer_active` changes (tray.rs:345-357).
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: re-sync the checked state after each click regardless of whether `buffer_active` changed).

title: Stale comments
claim: Stale comments: the `shared` field doc says `save_clip` holds `pipeline` across ffmpeg; "stopping waits for a save in progress"; the console hotkey thread comment; tray.rs "several times a second"; "Reassign the two global hotkeys" (there are five).
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: update or remove the stale comments).

title: Missing tests for fullscreen heuristic, games.json merge and AutoBuffer automation
claim: game.rs's naming tests are meaningful, but there are no tests for the fullscreen heuristic, the games.json merge, or `AutoBuffer::poll`, `poll_always` and the manual-action interplay, which is exactly where the retry-storm (ST-3), Stream Deck bypass (ST-5) and alt-tab suppression (ST-9) bugs sit. Only `poll_lock` and `assigned_game` are tested.
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: add tests for these areas; make `track_game` pure to enable it).

title: from_exe does not trim an upper-case ".EXE" suffix
claim: `from_exe` does not trim ".EXE" in upper case when deriving a name from the executable.
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: trim the extension case-insensitively).

title: lib.rs is 1385 lines
claim: lib.rs is 1385 lines and mixes notify/actions, hotkeys, the status loop and setup.
fix: Split into notify/actions, hotkeys, status loop and setup modules.

title: German text mixed into an English codebase, including user-facing log lines
claim: German is mixed into an English codebase, including user-facing log lines: "Overlay bleibt klickbar", "Unbekannter Tray-Eintrag", "Pegel:", "blieb liegen", "Taktgeber", "Mischer".
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: translate to English).

title: SourceKind::Leftovers has no TypeScript counterpart
claim: `SourceKind::Leftovers` in model.rs has no counterpart in src/lib/types.ts; it is only read and is migrated at load.
fix: None proposed.

title: Banner.avatar and corner are always sent but optional in TS
claim: `Banner.avatar` and `corner` are always sent by Rust but typed as optional in src/lib/types.ts.
fix: None proposed.

title: UpdateProgress.finished exists only in TS
claim: `UpdateProgress.finished` exists only in TS, and is handled with `Omit<…>`.
fix: None proposed.

title: UWP games behind applicationframehost.exe are never detected
claim: UWP games run behind `applicationframehost.exe`, which game detection ignores, so UWP games are never detected.
fix: No explicit fix in the report (see the Xbox Game Bar / full-path detection proposals).

title: AppState is a god object with fragmented game-tracking locks and two sources of truth for capture state
claim: AppState mixes config persistence, capture lifecycle, game tracking, automation, file naming, and building `Clip` (written out three times: state.rs:859, 941, 1123); `now_ms` is duplicated. Seven game-tracking mutexes are always updated together, which forces a "one lock at a time" dance, and `game_for` reads three locks separately and can get an inconsistent picture. `status.buffer_active` and `is_buffering()` are two sources of truth for capture state. `track_game` is not a pure, testable function.
fix: Make the seven game-tracking mutexes one `Mutex<GameTracker>`; move pipeline, recorder, buffer_wanted, active_recording and `lifecycle` into a `CaptureController` with a single state enum; make `track_game` a pure, testable function.

title: Stream Deck "stop" while the buffer is already off still announces "Replay buffer stopped"
claim: A Stream Deck "stop" while the buffer is already off still plays "Replay buffer stopped" with sound and banner (stop is not idempotent / does not check current state).
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: idempotent `set_buffer(on)` as in the capture state machine proposal).

title: exe_name uses a MAX_PATH buffer, so games at longer paths are never detected
claim: `exe_name` uses a MAX_PATH-sized buffer (game.rs:408), so executables with longer paths are never detected.
fix: No explicit fix in the report (implied: support paths longer than MAX_PATH).

title: tao's set_focus can inject a synthetic Alt press via SendInput
claim: tao's `set_focus` falls back to injecting a synthetic Alt press via `SendInput` when `SetForegroundWindow` fails, which some anti-cheats flag (speculative).
fix: No explicit fix in the report.

title: Starting a second instance rotates and destroys the running instance's log
claim: lib.rs:1153: `logging::init()` runs before `.plugin(tauri_plugin_single_instance…)`. Plugin setup only runs at `.build()`, and `.manage(AppState::new())` (lib.rs:1185) is also evaluated eagerly before that. `rotate()` (logging.rs:59-63) renames the live `clippiboy.log` over `clippiboy.log.1`, destroying the previous session's log, then creates a new file. Rust opens files with share-delete, so the rename succeeds while the first instance has the log open. The second instance also loads config, enumerates MFT encoders (`encode::resolve`), runs SQLite migrations with no busy_timeout against the live database, and starts audio streams before it exits. Report severity: Medium-High.
fix: Do the single-instance check first (a named mutex in `main()` before `logging::init`, or a lazy `AppState`), and rotate only once this is known to be the primary instance.

title: Duplicate start/stop actions while one is still in progress (decisions taken outside lifecycle)
claim: `buffer_active` only becomes true at the end of `launch_pipeline`, so any 2 s automation tick during a slow start (cold boot, or `Pipeline::start` taking up to 10 s) spawns another Start (lib.rs:660). That thread waits on `lifecycle`, sees the pipeline running and returns Ok, producing a second "Replay buffer running" toast, sound and banner, plus another device enumeration. `toggle_buffer_and_notify` (lib.rs:335) and the `start_buffer`/`stop_buffer` commands also decide outside the lock; both commands are implemented as toggles (commands.rs:326-348), so a race can act in the wrong direction. `AutoBuffer` is five separate atomics, so `manual_stop` can tear against `poll` between its load of `suppressed` and its store to `started`.
fix: An "in-flight" flag or `lifecycle.try_lock()` in `apply_auto_buffer`; an idempotent `set_buffer(on)` checked under `lifecycle`; `AutoBuffer` as one `Mutex<AutoState>`.

title: Game detection treats maximized windows as fullscreen games
claim: game.rs:453-456 checks `rect.left <= screen.left && rect.top <= screen.top && rect.right >= screen.right && rect.bottom >= screen.bottom` against `rcMonitor`. A maximized framed window's `GetWindowRect` hangs about 8 px past the work area on every side. On a monitor with no taskbar (common on secondary screens) or with an auto-hide taskbar, the work area is the whole monitor, so any maximized unknown app counts as a fullscreen game (blender.exe, photoshop.exe, unity.exe, mstsc.exe, …).
fix: Require `!IsZoomed(hwnd)` and no `WS_CAPTION`/`WS_THICKFRAME`, or use `SHQueryUserNotificationState` (QUNS_BUSY or D3D fullscreen).

title: Heavy sync Tauri commands block the UI thread
claim: These commands are sync, so they run on the main thread: `set_config` (stops and restarts the pipeline on a source change, commands.rs:117-121), `list_encoders` (MFT enumeration), `list_capture_targets` (EnumWindows + QueryDisplayConfig), `list_audio_devices` and `list_audio_processes` (COM). `file_clip` holds the library lock across `filing::place`, whose rename retries sleep up to 600 ms in total. `delete_clip` does file I/O; `set_clip_dir` writes a probe file, which can stall on a network path.
fix: `#[tauri::command(async)]` for all of these.

title: Status loop mixes 20 Hz UI work with slow polling, and polling is costly
claim: The status thread (`spawn_ui_updates`, lib.rs:928) runs one 50 ms loop forever (no stop flag, no join) that mixes 20 Hz UI work with slow polling, so any stall freezes the meters, game detection and the automation together (e.g. `refresh_free_bytes` on a dead network drive, or COM `list_devices` on a bad audio driver). Per 2 s tick: `QueryDisplayConfig` twice (watch_monitors, screen_drift) — frequent display-config polling is a reported cause of periodic stutter on some drivers (speculative); `OpenInputDesktop` three times; endpoint enumeration plus property stores; a freshly spawned thread doing a Toolhelp snapshot with one String per process, plus audio session enumeration; foreground detection with a second `OpenProcess` in `foreground_is_ours`. Per 50 ms: `config_snapshot().sources` clones the whole `AppConfig` (lib.rs:946), and `std::env::var("CLIPPIBOY_LOG_LEVELS")` is looked up (lib.rs:963).
fix: Separate threads for meters and monitoring; an `Arc<AppConfig>` swapped on change; event-driven sources (see proposals).

title: Two stop requests for one recording produce a spurious "Recording failed" banner
claim: lib.rs:1043-1048 spawns `stop_recording_and_notify` every second while `recording_failure()` is Some, with no guard; only `guard_recording_room` uses `STOPPING`. Both conditions fire together when the disk fills. The losing thread returns "No recording is running." and plays an error sound and banner on top of "Saving recording…". Report severity: Low-Medium; likely in the disk-full case.
fix: A shared stopping flag, or make the failure report one-shot.

title: Alt+F4 on the console destroys it for the rest of the session
claim: lib.rs:1276-1280 only prevents close for the `"main"` window. The console takes focus, so Alt+F4 destroys it. After that, `console::open` logs "console window missing" until the app restarts. Report severity: Low-Medium; confirmed by Tauri semantics.
fix: Prevent close for the console and call `console::close`, or recreate it lazily in `open()`.

title: tint.rs:36 panics on a non-ASCII accent colour (release build aborts on every start)
claim: tint.rs:36: `u8::from_str_radix(&hex[at..at + 2], 16)` runs after a byte-length check only, so the byte slice can split a multi-byte character and panic; `"#€ab1"` passes the check and panics (confirmed by test). `config::load` does not call `clean_accent` (only `set_config` does), so a bad value from config.json reaches `tray::build`. Release builds abort on panic. Report severity: Low-Medium.
fix: `if !hex.is_ascii() { return None }`, and sanitize the accent in `load`.

title: Stream Deck start/stop bypass the automation's "user decided" flags
claim: control.rs:225-226 call `"start" => crate::start_buffer_and_notify(app)` and `"stop" => crate::stop_buffer_and_notify(app)` directly, with no `auto.manual_start()` / `manual_stop()` call, so the buffer automation does not know the user decided.
fix: Route through one `set_buffer(app, on, Origin::User)`.

title: Failed recording close leaves status.recording = true and an orphaned capture pipeline running
claim: state.rs:1072-1078: `Err(err) => { log::error!(…); return None; }` returns before `if !self.buffer_wanted() { self.halt_pipeline(); }` and before `self.status.lock().recording = false`. The recorder has already been removed from both AppState and the pipeline. `finish` fails when `write_meta` fails, which is exactly the disk-full case the room guard is there for.
fix: A scope guard that always halts the pipeline (when the buffer is not wanted) and clears the recording flag.

title: Quit does not wait for a save in progress and can hang on the main thread
claim: tray.rs:139-148 Quit runs `abandon_recording(); stop_pipeline(); app.exit(0)`, and so does the updater's `on_before_exit`. None of them check `is_saving()`. The save thread dies while ffmpeg is running (there is no Job object). In addition, the Quit handler runs on the main thread and joins encoder threads with no timeout.
fix: Do Quit on a worker thread: show a "finishing clip…" banner, wait for saving to clear with a timeout, then exit. Optionally handle WM_QUERYENDSESSION so a Windows logoff closes recordings cleanly.

title: "Only buffer in game": an alt-tab of 30 s or more cancels the user's manual stop, contradicting the README
claim: `poll` is fed `GameTick::playing`, which depends on what is in the foreground. state.rs:195-200: after `GRACE_POLLS` checks without the game in front, `self.suppressed.store(false, SeqCst)`. The README says the automation "holds back until the game has ended".
fix: Clear `suppressed` only when the bound game process exits (`game_pid` becomes None); consider pausing rather than stopping while the game process is still alive.

title: Suspension is not enforced on existing sessions, and a banned user can erase their own ban via DELETE /me
claim: authenticate() in server/src/db.ts:129-147 selects only `user_id, last_used` from `sessions` and never looks at `users.banned_at`. The only ban checks are at index.ts:198 (new sign-ins) and links.ts:182 (`createShare`). `live()` at links.ts:139-144 does not consider whether the share owner is banned, and `putPoster` has no ban check. `deleteAccount` at index.ts:383-391 runs `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?`, which removes `banned_at` along with the row, so the next Discord login creates a fresh account through `upsertDiscordUser`. `closeAll(reason)` at hub.ts:178 is only ever called from `deleteAccount`; there are no admin/moderation HTTP endpoints (moderation is done by hand with `wrangler d1 execute`), so nothing runs `Hub.closeAll` or deletes sessions when someone is suspended. A suspended user keeps a working session, presence, relays, friend requests, live share links/media and poster swaps; only `POST /shares` is refused.
fix: In db.ts authenticate: `SELECT s.user_id, s.last_used, u.banned_at FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id WHERE s.token_hash = ?`; `if (!s || now - s.last_used > SESSION_IDLE_MS) throw new HttpError(401, ...)`; `if (s.banned_at !== null) throw new HttpError(403, "This account is suspended.")`. In links.ts live(): `... FROM shares s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.owner WHERE s.id = ? AND u.banned_at IS NULL`. Keep bans outside `users` (a `banned_discord_ids` table checked in `authCallback` before the upsert), or refuse `DELETE /me` while banned, or keep a minimal row. Add a cron 'suspension apply' step: find users with `banned_at` set and `suspended_applied_at IS NULL`, delete their sessions, take down their shares (R2 + tombstone), and call `HUB.getByName(id).closeAll("suspended")` (avoids a new admin HTTP surface). Also check the ban in `putPoster`.

title: A 60-second Hub alarm per online user burns the Free-plan Durable Object request quota
claim: The Hub arms a 60-second alarm per online user (hub.ts:33,76,135). Alarm invocations count as Durable Object requests: 1,440 per day for each always-online user.
fix: Sweep every 5 minutes, or skip re-arming when every socket was auto-pinged recently.

title: POST /t/ping is unauthenticated and unthrottled; each fresh-UUID ping writes ~6 D1 rows kept 400 days, exhausting the shared daily write quota
claim: `POST /t/ping` (telemetry.ts:83-111) has no rate limit; the only check is the body shape. Each ping with a fresh random UUIDv4 inserts into `installs` and `install_days`; counting their PK and secondary indexes, that is roughly 6 D1 'rows written' per request, and the rows are kept 400 days. The D1 database and its Free-plan daily limits (about 100k rows written, 5M rows read) are shared by the whole app.
fix: Add a rate-limit binding `PING_LIMIT` keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP` (for example 5/60 s), as `REPORT_LIMIT` already does without storing the address. Turn off `workers_dev`, or WAF rules can be bypassed through it. Optionally drop pings whose `version` is not a known release.

title: GET /auth/start is unthrottled and runs a full-table DELETE on logins (no created_at index), so D1 reads grow quadratically
claim: Each unauthenticated `GET /auth/start` (index.ts:139-143) runs `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?`, and `logins` has no index on `created_at`, so every request scans the whole table. It then runs an INSERT that touches the table plus 2 unique indexes. There is no rate limit. R requests inside 10 minutes cost about R^2/2 rows read.
fix: Add an `AUTH_LIMIT` rate-limit binding keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP`. `CREATE INDEX logins_created ON logins(created_at)`, and move the logins cleanup into the cron. Turn off `workers_dev` so WAF rules cannot be bypassed.

title: Privacy page: suspension promise ('signed out ... links are taken down') is not implemented
claim: The privacy page says: "A suspended account is signed out, cannot sign in or share links, and its links are taken down." Only 'cannot sign in again' and 'cannot create links' are implemented. Existing sessions, sockets, relays, live links and poster swaps keep working, and the ban disappears on `DELETE /me` (same root cause as SV-1).
fix: Implement the promise (see SV-1 fix) or change the wording.

title: Share pages reveal the uploader's Discord user ID via the avatar URL
claim: db.ts:88 builds the avatar URL as `https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/${user.id}/${hash}.png`, and page.ts:116 puts it into the public share page whenever `show_name` is set (the default, which users opt out of), exposing the Discord snowflake user ID. The privacy page only says 'display name and avatar'. Also, `show_name` is frozen at upload time, so turning the setting off later does not hide the name on links that are already live.
fix: Proxy the avatar through a route such as `/c/:id/avatar`, or use the default avatar, or disclose it.

title: The e2e script seeds known bearer tokens into the production database
claim: scripts/e2e.mjs:11-21 defaults `BASE` to the production workers.dev address and seeds fixed tokens `tok-a-test-only` / `tok-b-test-only` and friend codes `AAAAAAAA` / `BBBBBBBB`, all in a public repo. Cleanup relies on a comment ('Remove the accounts afterwards').
fix: Generate random tokens at seed time and print them; default to a local `wrangler dev`; give the seeded rows a short `last_used` expiry or a cleanup cron.

title: Two users sending each other friend requests at the same moment get a 500
claim: In the friend-request handler (index.ts:326-342), both concurrent requests pass the `existing` check, and the second INSERT into `friendships` hits the (ordered pair) primary key, returning 500.
fix: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(user_a, user_b) DO UPDATE SET status='accepted' WHERE requester <> excluded.requester`, then re-read the row.

title: Presence can arrive at friends out of order
claim: `publish` at hub.ts:219-237 awaits D1 and RPCs, which opens the Durable Object's input gate, so two quick hello/presence messages can interleave. Friends may receive the older presence last and keep showing it.
fix: Add a sequence number or `at` to `friendPresence` and have receivers drop older ones; or serialize `publish` through a promise chain.

title: Media is publicly cacheable for up to an hour after deletion, and not marked noindex
claim: links.ts:395 sends `public, max-age=min(left, 3600)` on media, so a deleted, moderated or account-deleted clip stays in browser and intermediary caches for up to an hour, although the page promises it is 'removed immediately'. Media responses have no `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and `api.clippiboy.com/robots.txt` returns 401.
fix: `private, max-age=300` or `no-cache` with an ETag, and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on media and on the gone page.

title: No 'sign out everywhere'
claim: Session lifecycle gap: there is no way to revoke all of a user's sessions ('sign out everywhere'); only `POST /auth/logout` for the current session exists.
fix: Add `DELETE /sessions`.

title: sweep runs its cleanup steps in sequence, so one R2 error skips the rest including the 30-day report deletion
claim: Within `sweep` (links.ts:419-448) the steps run in sequence without per-step error handling, so an R2 error skips the stale-upload cleanup, the tombstone purge, and the 30-day report deletion (a privacy-page promise).
fix: Wrap each step on its own.

title: Usernames are only synced at login, so two users rows can share a username after a Discord rename
claim: Usernames are only synced at login (db.ts:93-119) and `username` is not unique, so after a Discord rename two rows can share a username.
fix: Make `username` unique and sync it on use.

title: Posters can be swapped any number of times
claim: `PUT /shares/:id/poster` (links.ts:273-289) lets the owner replace the poster (the `og:image` in Discord and Twitter embeds) with any JPEG, any number of times, with no limit.
fix: Allow one poster PUT per share, or a few at most.

title: Privacy page: usage stats called 'anonymous' are actually pseudonymous
claim: The privacy page says usage stats are 'anonymous', with an installation number 'not linked to you'. In practice it is pseudonymous: a persistent installation ID with a per-day profile kept up to 400 days. A unique `/get/<ref>` handed to a single person would identify them.
fix: Either commit to never issuing per-person refs, or say 'pseudonymous'.

title: Spec: 'no public counting route anyone could call' contradicted by /get/<ref>
claim: The spec says there is 'no public counting route anyone could call'. `/get/<ref>` is itself that route, and its counts can be forged freely. The spec accepts fake pings but not fake downloads.
fix: Rate-limit or otherwise protect `/get` counting (see SV-4), or update the spec.

title: Missing tests: auth flow (state mismatch, code reuse, expiry, verifier, bans)
claim: Today's 25 tests only cover pure functions. There are no integration tests (e.g. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers or Miniflare with real D1, R2 and Durable Objects) for the auth flow: cookie/state mismatch, code reuse, expired login, wrong verifier, banned user at callback and on every authenticated route, and `DELETE /me` while banned.
fix: Add these tests with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers or Miniflare.

title: Missing tests: upload quota race and upload edge cases
claim: No test covers the upload quota race (N parallel uploads), abandoned pending uploads, a body shorter or longer than its Content-Length, or that a non-MP4 gives 415 and leaves no R2 object behind.
fix: Add integration tests for these cases.

title: Hourly sweepUsage does a full scan of installs because installs.last_day has no index
claim: The hourly cron `sweepUsage` (telemetry.ts:119) runs `DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?`. `installs.last_day` has no index, so this is a full table scan every hour (rows read = install count x 24 per day). Fake pings via the unthrottled `/t/ping` inflate it further.
fix: `CREATE INDEX installs_last_day ON installs(last_day)`, and run `sweepUsage` once a day.

title: Missing tests: share page rendering and response headers
claim: No snapshot test of `renderPage` with hostile title, game, tags and uploader name, plus the response headers (`nosniff`, cache, CSP once added).
fix: Add a snapshot test with hostile inputs and header assertions.

title: Missing tests: sweep
claim: No test covers the sweep: expired, stale-pending and tombstone purge; partial R2 failure; reports past 30 days; the usage cutoff boundary.
fix: Add integration tests for the sweep steps.

title: Missing CSP, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and no-store headers on share and sign-in pages
claim: The share page (links.ts:372) and the auth pages (index.ts:242) send no Content-Security-Policy, `frame-ancestors` or `Referrer-Policy`. The callback page carries the one-time code but has no `Cache-Control: no-store`. Escaping is correct, so this is defence in depth only.
fix: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'sha256-…'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src https://api.clippiboy.com https://cdn.discordapp.com; media-src https://api.clippiboy.com; font-src https://clippiboy.com; connect-src https://api.clippiboy.com; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `Cache-Control: no-store` on the callback page.

title: Idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but never deleted
claim: Session lifecycle gap: idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but the `sessions` rows are never deleted (no sweep); they are kept until the account is deleted.
fix: Have the cron delete stale sessions.

title: logins rows (user_id + one-time code) are only cleaned up on the next /auth/start
claim: Session lifecycle gap: `logins` rows, which hold `user_id` and the one-time code, are only cleaned up when someone next calls `/auth/start` (the `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` there); there is no cron cleanup.
fix: Have the cron delete stale logins.

title: Cron uses Promise.all inside waitUntil, so a sweep rejection can cut sweepUsage short
claim: The scheduled handler at index.ts:45 runs `sweep` and `sweepUsage` with `Promise.all` inside `waitUntil`: if `sweep` rejects, the invocation may end while `sweepUsage` is still running.
fix: Use `Promise.allSettled`.

title: Account deletion fails for accounts with more than 500 live links
claim: At links.ts:305 account deletion removes all live shares' R2 objects in one R2 `delete` call. More than 500 live shares means more than 1,000 keys in one call, which throws, so `DELETE /me` returns 500. Only reachable for accounts with `unlimited_links` or `QUICK_LINKS_FOR`.
fix: Delete in chunks of 1,000 keys.

title: Expiry rounding overstates the time left
claim: shares.ts:98 computes the expiry text with `Math.round(left / DAY_MS)`, which rounds up partial days.
fix: Use `Math.floor` for days, and show hours below 2 days.

title: The site proxy is not covered by npm run check
claim: The site proxy is not type-checked by `npm run check`, because the tsconfig only includes `src`.
fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: include the site proxy in the type check.

title: Privacy page: 'No cookies' while api.clippiboy.com sets cb_login
claim: The privacy page says 'No cookies.', but `api.clippiboy.com` sets the `cb_login` cookie during sign-in. It is strictly necessary, so this is a wording issue.
fix: Reword the privacy page to mention the strictly necessary sign-in cookie.

title: Missing tests: expiresIn boundaries
claim: No test covers `expiresIn` at 12 h, 36 h and 4.5 days.
fix: Add unit tests at these boundaries.

title: Report handling: reports never surfaced, owner can destroy evidence, clips expire unreviewed, reports forgeable cross-site
claim: (1) Reports filed via `POST /c/:id/report` are never surfaced to anyone; the operator has to poll D1. (2) The owner can delete a reported clip (`deleteShare` wipes it from R2 and blanks the title), which destroys the evidence. (3) Clips expire after 5 days whether or not anyone reviewed them. (4) Any website can make its visitors' browsers file reports (no-cors `text/plain` POST); the rate limit (`REPORT_LIMIT`, 5/min) is per IP and per Cloudflare location, and IPv6 rotation gets around it.
fix: Hide a clip automatically after N distinct-IP reports, notify the operator (webhook or email), and move reported objects to a quarantine prefix instead of deleting them.

title: A null or non-object JSON body gives a 500
claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 casts the parsed JSON without validating that it is an object, and callers destructure the result (for example index.ts:212), so a `null` or non-object body throws and returns 500.
fix: Have `body()` reject anything that is not an object; check `typeof code === "string"`.

title: Media Range and conditional request handling is wrong (bad ranges return 206 full body, If-None-Match ignored, HEAD reads body)
claim: Media serving at links.ts:383-406 passes Range through without validation: `bytes=999999-`, `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and multi-range requests return 206 with the whole object instead of 416 or 200 (production R2 may throw instead, surfacing as the generic 500). `If-None-Match` is ignored (always 200), and HEAD downloads the object body (an R2 Class B operation).
fix: Parse `Range` yourself; return 416 if `start >= size` and 200 when the range is unparseable; pass `onlyIf: request.headers` and return 304; use `CLIPS.head()` for HEAD.

title: Logout and suspension do not close an already-open WebSocket
claim: Session lifecycle gap: the bearer token is only checked when the `/ws` socket connects (index.ts:82-91), so logout and suspension do not close a socket that is already open.
fix: Call `closeAll` on logout of the last session or on suspension.

title: The MP4 checker has no cap on box count (CPU exhaustion)
claim: The MP4 box checker at shares.ts:173-216 iterates boxes with no limit on how many top-level boxes a file may contain.
fix: Refuse files with more than about 100k top-level boxes.

title: Friend requests: no rate limit or pending cap, and 404 vs 403 responses enable user enumeration
claim: `POST /friends/request` (index.ts:313-345) has no rate limit and no cap on outgoing pending requests, and Discord usernames can be guessed. The response distinguishes 404 (no such user, or they blocked you) from 403 (allow_requests is off), which reveals which Discord accounts use ClippiBoy.
fix: Rate-limit; cap outgoing pending requests at around 20; return the same answer for 403 and 404.

title: Site proxy GET /get/<ref> lets any browser-UA client add D1 writes to the shared database, with unbounded new refs kept 400 days
claim: In the site proxy, `/get[/ref]` (site-proxy/index.ts:67-75) adds +1 to `downloads(day, ref)` in the same D1 database whenever the request is a GET from a non-bot User-Agent, with no rate limit. `ref` is any `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, so every new ref creates a row kept 400 days. The count happens even if the client aborts right after the headers.
fix: Add a rate-limit binding or a WAF rule for `/get` in the site proxy; optionally cap distinct refs per day.

title: Privacy page: 'does not store your IP address' may be undermined by invocation logs
claim: The privacy page says 'Our server does not store your IP address with it.' That is true for D1, but `observability.enabled` (wrangler.jsonc:8) turns on invocation logs, which may record request metadata (time, path `/t/ping`, possibly IP and headers) for some days.
fix: Consider turning invocation logs off or excluding `/t/ping`.

title: Privacy page: 'database is located in Western Europe' unverifiable; Hub DO storage not pinned to EU

claim: The privacy page says deleting the account removes everything 'immediately'. Media can survive in caches for up to an hour (`public, max-age`); `logins` rows stay until the next sign-in start; reports referencing the share IDs stay 30 days (they hold no personal data).

title: The download endpoint trusts release.setup.url without pinning it
claim: site-proxy/index.ts:61 streams whatever URL `release.json` (read from Pages) names in `release.setup.url`, served as `ClippiBoy_<v>_x64-setup.<ref>.exe` from clippiboy.com, without validating the URL origin or the version format.

title: Privacy page: share links say 'display name and avatar' but also expose the Discord user ID
claim: The privacy page says share links show 'display name and avatar'. The avatar URL also exposes the Discord user ID (same issue as SV-10).
fix: Proxy or replace the avatar, or disclose it (see SV-10).

title: Hub Durable Object: unlimited sockets per user, no rate limit on hello/presence, relay budget is per connection
claim: `acceptWebSocket` at hub.ts:66 has no cap on sockets per user. The relay budget (intended 30 per 10 s) lives in `this.relayed`, keyed per WebSocket (hub.ts:248-252), so more sockets multiply it. Every `hello` or `presence` message (hub.ts:89-98) runs `sendSnapshot`, then `publish`: a Durable Object storage write, a D1 `friendIds` query, and one RPC to each friend's Hub, which in turn sends to every one of that friend's sockets; there is no rate limit on these messages. Every relay does a D1 `areFriends` lookup (hub.ts:256), even when the result is 'not a friend'.
fix: Cap sockets per user (e.g. close the oldest beyond 5). Apply one per-connection budget to all message types and close the socket with code 4008 on abuse. Keep the per-user relay budget in `ctx.storage` or in memory per user, not per socket. Cache the friend set in the Hub, invalidated by `friendsChanged`, so relays do not hit D1. Coalesce `publish` calls (debounce about 1 s).

title: 'Appear offline' can be detected through a relay probe
claim: `relay()` at hub.ts:158-162 delivers to every `ready` socket and returns true without checking `attachment.invisible`, so the sender only gets `relayFailed: "offline"` when the target has truly no sockets. An invisible user is therefore distinguishable from an offline one, contradicting the privacy page promise: "With 'Appear offline', friends see you as offline."
fix: If `this.current() === null` (invisible or offline), do not deliver and answer "offline". Alternatively, have the app opt in per relay. Either way the answer must look the same.

title: Unbounded request bodies are read into memory, including on unauthenticated routes
claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 calls `request.json()` with no size limit; it is used by `/auth/exchange` (unauthenticated), `/me` PATCH and `/friends/request`. At telemetry.ts:85-87 the size check relies on Content-Length, which is absent in chunked uploads, then calls `request.text()`. links.ts:324 does `JSON.parse((await request.text()).slice(0, 2048))`, reading everything and then slicing. `putPoster` already guards against this (see its comment at links.ts:276), but these routes do not.
fix: A shared `readLimited(request, max)` that streams with `getReader()`, cancels and returns 413 once `max` is passed, and rejects when Content-Length exceeds `max`. Validate that the parsed JSON is an object (this also fixes the null-body 500).

title: A few throwaway accounts can keep the global share bucket 'full' with abandoned pending uploads
claim: shares.ts:18 sets `TOTAL_BYTES = 9 GB` with `WEEKLY_LIMIT = 3` per account. At links.ts:57 a pending upload holds its declared `bytes` for up to 30 minutes, and an aborted upload is deleted (links.ts:252), so it does not use up a weekly slot. Reservations can be re-opened repeatedly at no quota cost.
fix: Count a pending reservation against the week even after it is abandoned (keep the row with `aborted = 1` instead of deleting it). Cap how many bytes a single account can have live. Alert on a full bucket. Consider a per-IP rate limit on `POST /shares`.

title: UI config copy goes stale: patchConfig sends the whole stale config and ignores the core's corrected reply
claim: patchConfig in src/store.ts:362-373 does `const config = { ...get().config, ...patch }; set({ config }); ... await api.setConfig(config);`, and src/lib/ipc.ts:47 types it as `setConfig: (config: AppConfig) => invoke<void>("set_config", { config })` (also listed under the report's IPC-contract-drift finding: setConfig is typed void but the command returns a config). The core command actually returns AppConfig (commands.rs:55-59) after rewriting it: while a recording runs, a source change is reverted and the core calls `crate::notify(&app, "error", "Stop the recording before changing the source.")` (commands.rs:72-81); the encoder is replaced by `encode::resolve(...)` (state.rs:367); accent colours are cleaned. The UI discards that reply and keeps (and later resends) its own uncorrected whole config. The core also edits the config on its own and never tells the UI: `repair_screens()` (lib.rs:472-507, called on monitor changes at lib.rs:542 and :586) rewrites `recording.target_id`, the overlay screen and the console screen; there is no `config-changed` event.
fix: 1) Type `set_config` as `invoke<AppConfig>` and apply the reply behind a version guard (same ticket pattern as `clips-changed` at store.ts:301): `const v = ++cfgVersion; const next = await api.setConfig(config); if (v === cfgVersion) set({ config: next });`. 2) Emit `config-changed` from the core after `repair_screens`, the tray hint and token changes, and listen for it in `init`. 3) Better: replace the whole-config write with a core-side merged `patch_config(patch)`.

title: Hotkey recorder cannot be started from the keyboard; recorder/Unbind buttons not tied to row labels
claim: In settings/Hotkeys.tsx:329-333 recording starts only on `onMouseDown`; Enter/Space fire `click`, not mousedown, so keyboard users cannot assign hotkeys. The recorder button and the "Unbind" buttons are not associated with their row labels.
fix: Add an `onClick`/`onKeyDown` path to start recording, and tie the recorder and Unbind buttons to their row labels.

title: Recording page selects have no labels

title: Mixer M/S/⧉ buttons and label input are unnamed and lack state

title: Gallery tile actions stay invisible when keyboard-focused

title: Dashboard clip cards and Stat cards are clickable divs without keyboard support

title: Menu opened by keyboard on Friends "More" appears top-left

title: Menu lacks Home/End/Tab handling and aria-activedescendant

title: --color-ink-faint fails WCAG AA contrast
claim: `--color-ink-faint: #5c5c68` measures 2.84:1 on surface, 2.63:1 on elevated and 3.04:1 on base, failing WCAG AA; it is used 83 times, mostly for small hint text.

title: Reduced-motion rule covers only cb-* animations

title: useLinks.refresh has no ticket and can race itself
claim: `useLinks.refresh` (links.ts:63) applies results without a ticket/version guard.

title: Text-field menu Paste into number inputs prepends and throws
claim: dom.ts:48 includes `"number"` in the text input types. In TextMenu.tsx:31-37, `selectionStart` is `null` for number inputs (treated as 0), so pasted text is prepended, and then `setSelectionRange` throws `InvalidStateError` (an unhandled rejection from the async `onSelect`). Paste also bypasses `maxLength`.

title: Record and buffer buttons have no in-flight guard

title: Memory-budget slider cannot return to automatic (0) once dragged

title: vite.config.ts is not type-checked

title: init() is not idempotent; listeners register twice and are never removed
claim: App.tsx:31-33 calls `void init()` in an effect, which StrictMode runs twice in dev. Every `listen()` in store.ts:272-332 registers twice and is never removed. In browser mode there are two 80 ms intervals (store.ts:228). Vite HMR repeats this for the module-level listeners in friends.ts, share.ts, links.ts and hidden.ts.

title: screenshotHasOriginal invokes an unregistered command (dead code)

title: ipc.ts hotkey doc says "All four at once" for five hotkeys
claim: The doc comment at ipc.ts:53-54 says "All four at once" while there are five hotkeys.
fix: Correct the comment.

title: lockdown.ts matches physical event.code, missing zoom shortcuts on QWERTZ
claim: `lockdown.ts` matches shortcuts on physical `event.code`, so on QWERTZ keyboards Ctrl+`+`/Ctrl+`-` (codes `BracketRight` and `Slash`) are not caught; it relies on Tauri's own zoom disable.

title: Menu re-subscribes five window listeners on every render
claim: The effect in Menu.tsx:143-192 depends on `selectable` and `run`, which are new on every render, so it removes and re-adds five window listeners on every render.
fix: Memoize `selectable`/`run` or read them through refs so the effect subscribes once.

title: SlidingIndicator transitions width
claim: `SlidingIndicator` transitions `width` (a layout property) rather than a transform.
fix: Animate with `transform` (scaleX/translateX) instead of width.

title: Main window keeps rendering and receiving 20 Hz IPC while the user is gaming
claim: tauri.conf.json:27 gives the main window `--disable-features=...CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding`; per overlay.rs:40-56 and the README these flags exist for the banner, which now has its own data dir and browser process. The core emits `audio-levels` to `main` at 20 Hz whenever the window is visible and not minimized (lib.rs:964-967), including when behind the game, and store.ts:272 does `set({ levels })` on every page even with no meter on screen; each `set` runs every subscriber's selector (the gallery has one per tile, `NameField`, Clips.tsx:707). NavBar.tsx:176 renders `<LiveDot />` whenever the buffer runs, an infinite animation (motion.css:132-134, `cb-live-ring 2s infinite`) inside a `backdropFilter: "blur(20px)"` pill (NavBar.tsx:49), so the compositor produces frames continuously and likely re-blurs each frame. In RGB accent mode accent.ts:157 runs `setInterval(refresh, 80)` rewriting 16 root custom properties (whole-document style recalc), gated only by `!document.hidden`, which does not change when the window is merely occluded once occlusion detection is off.
fix: 1) Drop the three occlusion/backgrounding flags from the main window. 2) Add a frontend "dormant" mode driven by `onHidden`, `blur`, `focus` from lib/hidden.ts: set `html[data-dormant]` with `[data-dormant] [class*="cb-"]{animation-play-state:paused}` and stop the accent interval. 3) Make levels opt-in (ref-counted `api.watchLevels(on)` while a `Meter` is mounted, or a separate tiny levels store). 4) Throttle RGB mode to 2-4 Hz or animate it with `filter: hue-rotate()` on the few accent surfaces.

title: Focus is lost to <body> when delete is swapped for ConfirmDelete
claim: Clicking delete swaps the trigger for `ConfirmDelete`, so the focused element disappears and focus falls to `<body>`.
fix: Move focus to ConfirmDelete's Cancel button (the safe default).

title: Sliders write every intermediate value; dragging the buffer slider discards footage
claim: The buffer-length slider in Recording.tsx:393-409 uses `onChange={(seconds) => patchConfig({ buffer: { ...config.buffer, seconds, ... } })}` and the memory-budget slider at Recording.tsx:468-477 does the same, so every intermediate drag value is written. The core applies each value immediately: state.rs:381-388 calls `shared.packets.lock().set_capacity(next.buffer.seconds, memory)` and buffer.rs:69-73 `set_capacity` calls `self.trim()`. The same per-move write pattern exists in Sounds.tsx:257-263 and :297-303 (100 steps), the console scale slider in Console.tsx:229-236, and the gain slider in AudioMixer.tsx:384-391 (`upsertSource` on every move).
fix: Give `Slider` a local draft value and an `onCommit` callback fired on `pointerup`/`keyup` (or `change`) and write only on commit; alternatively reuse the `SETTLE_MS` debounce from Colors.tsx:29-34. On the core side, debounce `config::save`.

title: No ESLint config although eslint-disable comments exist; floating promises go undetected
claim: The repo has no ESLint config, yet five `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` comments exist (ClipPlayer.tsx:210, Setup.tsx:128, Share.tsx:295, ShotViewer.tsx:362, :414). Without `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`, floating promises such as `upsertSource(s);` (AudioMixer.tsx:242) and `inTauri && api.revealClip()` (Clips.tsx:602) go unflagged.
fix: Add a flat ESLint config with `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` (recommended-latest) and `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, and enable `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`.

title: tsconfig lacks noUncheckedIndexedAccess (51 errors when enabled)

title: Friends route reports errors through a window CustomEvent
