fix: Route errors through a store-level notify function.

title: Outdated comment in store.ts about saving on every keystroke
claim: The comment at store.ts:490 about saving on every keystroke is outdated; `ClipMeta` now saves on blur.
fix: Update or remove the comment.

title: Meter keeps a 60 ms interval forever and animates width
claim: `Meter` (Controls.tsx:163-197) keeps a 60 ms `setInterval` per meter for its whole lifetime and animates `width`, which triggers layout.
fix: Use a ref plus `transform: scaleX` driven by requestAnimationFrame.

title: Tray icon sent as a 64 KB JSON number array
claim: accent.ts:142 sends the 64 KB tray icon to the core as a JSON number array (`Array.from(pixels)`).
fix: Send the pixels as binary.

title: Keyboard reorder in the mixer loses focus after one step
claim: `nudge` with ArrowDown (AudioMixer.tsx:201-208) makes React move the focused row's DOM node, so focus is lost after one step.
fix: Re-focus the grip after the move.

title: Clip gallery is unvirtualized and unmemoized; each tile pays for an uncached toLocaleDateString
claim: format.ts:24 does `new Date(ts).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` once per tile per render (Clips.tsx:625); measured in Node/V8 at 63-81 ms per 1000 calls versus about 1 ms with a cached `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. `visible` (Clips.tsx:199-225) and every tile are rebuilt inline on every render (each search keystroke, `clips-changed`, `links` change, rename or confirm-state change). Each tile carries 2-4 `Pill`s with `backdrop-blur-md` (Card.tsx:38) plus heart/action buttons with `backdrop-blur-md` (Clips.tsx:557, :1180), so hundreds of backdrop-filter surfaces re-blur while scrolling. On first visit every tile, including off-screen ones, gets `cb-tile-in`.
fix: Hoist `const DATE = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...)` in format.ts; extract a `ClipTile` wrapped in `React.memo` with stable id-keyed callbacks and memoize `visible` with `useMemo([clips, query, filter])`; add `content-visibility:auto; contain-intrinsic-size:auto 300px` to tiles or virtualize rows (e.g. `@tanstack/react-virtual`), so `useFlip` animates only mounted rows; replace `backdrop-blur` on tile chrome with solid `bg-black/60`; pass `updateClip` into `NameField` instead of subscribing per tile.

title: Mixer source label saves on every keystroke; a stale reply can drop typed characters
claim: AudioMixer.tsx:333-337 has `onChange={(e) => upsertSource({ ...source, label: e.target.value })}`, and store.ts:418-423 then does `set({ config: await api.updateAudioSource(source) })` unconditionally (last reply wins, no version guard). The same last-reply-wins problem affects gain, mute and solo.
fix: Keep a draft label and commit on blur/Enter, as `NameField` already does (Clips.tsx:697-771). Add the version guard from FC-1 to `upsertSource`/`removeSource`.

title: Mock data is the real store's initial config and its fallback in Tauri mode
claim: store.ts:164 initialises the store with `config: mock.mockConfig`, and store.ts:263 loads with `load("Reading the settings", api.getConfig, get().config)`, i.e. the mock config is the fallback if `get_config` fails, also in Tauri mode.
fix: Use `config: AppConfig | null` (or a `loaded` flag), don't render config-dependent routes until loaded, never fall back to mock in Tauri, and make `patchConfig` refuse to run before load.

title: Errors only show at the bottom of Settings and are never cleared
claim: Every failing store action calls `set({ lastError })` (`updateClip`, `setFavorite`, `setClipTags`, `patchConfig`, `clearGame`, `toggleBuffer`, `refreshTargets` and others), but `lastError` is only displayed in settings/index.tsx:80-84, and nothing ever sets `lastError: null` after the initial state (store.ts:188).
fix: Add a store-level `notify(kind, msg)` that feeds `Toasts` (which should also get `role="status"`/`aria-live`). Make `lastError` dismissible, or drop it.

title: Clearing a game makes one IPC write per clip and change events undo the optimistic update mid-loop
claim: `clearGame` in store.ts:570-578 loops `await api.updateClip(...)` then `await get().fileClip(...)` per clip. Each `update_clip` runs `announce_change`, which emits `clips-changed` (commands.rs:941), and the listener at store.ts:302-310 re-reads the full clip list each time.
fix: Add a single `clear_game(game)` core command that runs in one transaction and announces once.

title: EngineStatus fields are dropped by the store and never shown
claim: The `EngineStatus` fields `droppedFrames`, `fps`, `freeBytes`, `gameSeconds` and `encoder` are dropped by store.ts:273-285 and never shown in the UI.
fix: Keep these fields in the store and surface them (e.g. a health panel).

title: Clips without audio, or whose track query failed, can never be trimmed
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:535 `const dirty = duration > 0 && mix.tracks.length > 0 && !sameEdit(...)` requires at least one track. stems.rs `tracks()` returns `in_file` (an empty list) when the file has no audio stream, and useClipMix.ts:163 turns a failed `clipTracks` call into an empty list (`.catch(() => undefined)`). Setup allows "no audio source" ("your clips are silent"); such clips, and any clip while ffprobe is unavailable (ffmpeg still downloading or failed), keep Save disabled forever. The editor then also says "This clip carries a single audio track" (ClipEditor.tsx:123), which is wrong when the query failed.
fix: Use `!mix.loading` instead of `tracks.length > 0`, and show a separate "Tracks could not be read" message on error.

title: A running Save/Undo-trim does not block paging, closing or deleting
claim: `save()` at ClipPlayer.tsx:547-582 (`resumeAt`, `veil.freeze`, `await applyClipEdit`, then in `finally` `setReload((n)=>n+1)` and `setJustSaved(true)`) runs while the keyboard handler (`n`/`p` -> `step`, Escape -> `close`), the Step buttons, Delete and the close button stay enabled. ClipPlayer.tsx:253 resets `justSaved` only when the clip changes, before the save finishes. Paging to clip B during A's save: B plays under A's frozen frame; when A finishes, `setJustSaved(true)` makes B show "Saved. That is how the clip sits in the folder now"; `setReload` re-creates B's `<video>` so B restarts; the editor shows "Saving..." for B and the progress bar stalls because the listener now filters on B's id. Closing during a save calls Clips.closePlayer, which runs `fileClip` while the edit job may be between ffmpeg and `swap_in`; deleting during a save runs `delete_clip` while `apply` runs. The core's render lock does not cover filing or deletion. (UI part confirmed; Rust races speculative.)
fix: While `saving || restoring`, disable step, close, delete and the shortcuts; alternatively key `saving` and `justSaved` by clip id and ignore results for a clip that is no longer shown.

title: Unsaved trim and mix are lost without warning on close or paging
claim: Closing and paging in ClipPlayer have no check of `dirty`: Escape, `n`/`p` or the close button drop a carefully set trim and mix, with only the "Not saved yet" line as warning. ShotViewer, by contrast, asks "Discard unsaved marks?". There is also no Ctrl+S save shortcut.
fix: Add a dirty guard (an inline "Discard changes?" chip, as ShotViewer has) for close, paging and delete, and a Ctrl+S save shortcut.

title: Any reload of the video element resets the unsaved trim via restoreTrim on loadedmetadata
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:756-759 runs `restoreTrim(clip.edit, length)` and then `if (restored) setTrim(restored)` on every `loadedmetadata`, and ClipPlayer.tsx:799 retries a failed load with `setReload(n+1)`. So whenever the source changes under the open player or a load error triggers a retry, the unsaved trim is overwritten and playback restarts. Example: the user hearts the same clip in the console; Console.tsx:752 calls `fileClip`; the rename succeeds (the asset protocol opens files per request with Rust's default share flags, which allow deletion); the store reloads with the new `clip.path`, the `<video>` src changes, `loadedmetadata` resets the trim. A single transient load error does the same.
fix: Restore the trim only on the first metadata load for a clip id, or after save and restore (use a "trimRestoredFor" ref).

title: Clip menu actions in the main window fail silently and give no success feedback
claim: Menu actions fire-and-forget promises: clipMenu.tsx:136 `onSelect: () => void api.openClip(clip.id)`, and likewise 170 (`copyClipImage`), 180 (`copyClipFile`), 209 (`clipboardWriteText`), 216 (`revealClip`); ClipPlayer.tsx:959 `onClick={() => inTauri && api.revealClip(clip.id)}`. There is no `unhandledrejection` handler anywhere. "Copy clip" when the file is missing rejects with "The clip file is no longer there." and nothing is shown; on success nothing confirms the copy (the console says "Copied - Ctrl+V in Discord"; the app says nothing).
fix: Route every menu action through a helper that shows a success toast or `lastError`.

title: Friends.tsx swallows errors
claim: Friends.tsx:78 swallows errors with `.catch(() => {})`, so failures are never shown.
fix: Show the error via a toast or `lastError` instead of swallowing it.

title: Dashboard player never files favorites on close
claim: The dashboard's ClipPlayer never files favorites when it closes; the gallery (Clips.tsx) does that in `closePlayer`, so behaviour differs between the two players.
fix: Reuse the Clips.tsx playlist/close logic (including `closePlayer` filing) through a shared hook.

title: Trim tolerance mismatch: UI says dirty/"Saved" for an end cut the core ignores
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:1069 compares with `Math.abs(x - y) <= 50` while edit.rs:43 uses `EDGE_TOLERANCE_MS: u64 = 250`. Trimming 60-250 ms off the end enables Save; the core treats it as uncut, and the reload restores the full range, while the UI said "Saved".
fix: Share one tolerance (250 ms) for `dirty`, the "trimmed" flag and the core.

title: Solo is a listening aid in the UI but is saved as mutes
claim: useClipMix.ts:391-401 builds the saved state with `muted: !audible(state, anySolo)`, so soloing a track and pressing Save permanently mutes every other track in the file (recoverable because stems remain, but surprising).
fix: Exclude solo from the saved state and from `dirty`, or label it clearly ("Solo is saved as mute").

title: Dragging a trim handle re-renders the whole player and editor on every pointer move
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:146 calls `onTrim(...)` on every `pointermove`, which calls `setTrim` in ClipPlayer; each change re-renders ClipPlayer, ClipEditor, ClipMeta, Tags and all TrackRows, and tears down and re-creates the rAF effect (deps `[playing, trim.start, trim.end, paint]`) and the keydown listener. The authors note WebView2 drops video frames when React renders at frame rate. The drag also does not handle `pointercancel` or use `setPointerCapture`.
fix: Keep the trim in a ref during the drag and paint the handles directly (as for the playhead), commit on `pointerup`; read trim from a ref inside the rAF loop and key handler; handle `pointercancel` and use `setPointerCapture`.

title: Tauri event listener leak in ClipPlayer when cleanup runs before listen() resolves
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:303-314 uses `.then((off) => { unlisten = off; }); return () => unlisten?.();`. If cleanup runs before `listen()` resolves (StrictMode, which `main.tsx` uses, or fast paging), the listener is never removed. ExportDialog.tsx:84-95 does this correctly.
fix: Add a `useTauriEvent(name, cb)` hook with a `cancelled` flag and use it everywhere.

title: Waveform CSS url() is unquoted
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:185 ``backgroundImage: `url(${waveform})` `` leaves the URL unquoted. `convertFileSrc` uses `encodeURIComponent`, which leaves `(` and `)` unescaped, so a path containing parentheses breaks the declaration.
fix: Write `` `url("${waveform}")` ``.

title: Scrubber slider lacks own key handling and live ARIA values
claim: The scrubber (PlayerControls.tsx:162-178) is `role="slider"` with `tabIndex={0}` but has no key handling of its own (it relies on the global arrow keys). `aria-valuenow` is a percentage that is not updated while playing (the rAF loop writes the DOM directly), and there is no `aria-valuetext`.
fix: Give the scrubber arrow keys and a time text (`aria-valuetext`).

title: Track mute/solo buttons have confusing or missing accessible names
claim: The track mute buttons flip both their label and `aria-pressed` (double state change), and the Solo buttons have no track context in their accessible name.
fix: Keep a stable label with `aria-pressed`, and include the track name in Solo labels.

title: Space on a focused button toggles playback instead of activating the button
claim: In the player, pressing Space while a button has focus toggles playback (global shortcut) instead of activating the focused button.
fix: Skip the global Space shortcut when a button or other interactive control is focused.

title: Setup step dots put aria-label on a plain div with no role
claim: The Setup step dots carry `aria-label` on a plain `div` with no role, so the label is not reliably exposed.
fix: Give the element an appropriate role (or use visually hidden text).

title: REC badge blink composites at 60 fps on the CPU for the whole recording
claim: The REC badge uses `cb-rec-blink 1.4s infinite` (overlay.css:321), a smooth animation that composites at 60 fps on the CPU for the whole recording.
fix: Use `steps(2)` or an opacity toggle.

title: Player volume and mute are not persisted
claim: Player volume and mute are not persisted (ClipPlayer.tsx:109, Console.tsx:1210); they reset each time.
fix: Add a small localStorage preference.

title: ClipPlayer.tsx is a 1100-line component duplicating logic with ShotViewer and ClipStage
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx is about 1100 lines. ShotViewer duplicates `LEAVE_MS`, the close animation and the `Step` component; ClipStage (console) re-implements paint, rAF, toggle and seek.
fix: Split into `useOpenCloseFlight` (shared with ShotViewer), `useVideoTransport` (playing, time, duration, rAF paint, toggle, seek, trim loop; shared with ClipStage), `usePlayerShortcuts` with a modal stack, `useSaveFlow` (save, restore, discard, veil, reload) and `FullscreenBar`.

title: Console.tsx is a 1500-line file with a ~1000-line Console() component
claim: Console.tsx is about 1500 lines; `Console()` alone is about 1000 lines.
fix: Split into `useConsoleLifecycle` (open/close tickets, `untilSized`, `finishClose`), `Dock`, `ClipsSheet`, `PerfSheet`, `ClipStage`.

title: Comments and some strings mix German and English
claim: Comments and some UI strings mix German and English (e.g. the German trim-handle aria-labels and `zuletzt()`).
fix: Standardise on one language for comments and strings.

title: Misleading comments about clip file locking ("fails quietly" and "let go of the file")
claim: Tauri's asset protocol opens files per range request (at most 1 MB) with Rust's default Windows share flags, which allow deletion, so open video elements do not lock clip files. The "let go of the file" step in save is therefore not needed for locking (only the `?v=` cache-busting is), and the console's comment that filing a clip open in the main window "fails quietly" is likely wrong: the move succeeds (see FP-11).
fix: Correct the comments to reflect that the move succeeds.

title: Close timeout scheduled inside a setState updater fires twice under StrictMode
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:191-195 schedules `goodbye.current = window.setTimeout(onClose, LEAVE_MS)` inside a `setLeaving` updater function. StrictMode calls updaters twice, so in development `onClose` fires twice.
fix: Move the timeout out of the updater.

title: Duplicated helpers: zuletzt() and three clock() copies
claim: `zuletzt()` (Friends.tsx:232) duplicates `lastSeenText`, and there are three `clock()` copies (PlayerControls, ClipEditor, Setup).
fix: Consolidate into shared helpers.

title: Setup finish does not mention that ffmpeg may still be missing
claim: Setup's finish step does not mention that ffmpeg may still be missing (downloading or failed).
fix: Mention ffmpeg status on the finish step.

title: Hidden console keeps an infinite CSS animation (and full-screen glow layer) running for the whole session over the game
claim: When the console closes, the dock is only faded to opacity 0 by `.cb-ui[data-leaving="true"] { animation: cb-fade-out 160ms ease-in both; pointer-events: none; }` (console.css:273) and stays mounted. Console.tsx:1025 renders `<LiveDot />` in the dock whenever the buffer is running, and its ring uses `.cb-live-ring { animation: cb-live-ring 2s var(--ease-out-soft) infinite; }` (motion.css:132), so the infinite animation keeps running while the console is hidden. The window is hidden with `ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)`; Tauri's hide never calls WebView2 `SetIsVisible(false)` (only `webview.hide()` would). The console runs with `--disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` and `CalculateNativeWinOcclusion` off, so nothing throttles it, and with `--disable-gpu` the frames are rasterised and composited on the CPU. The full-screen `.cb-glow` layer (`will-change: opacity`) also stays alive. Related: the main window has the same flags, so any infinite animation it shows (e.g. LiveDot) also runs while it sits in the tray.
fix: After the exit animation (`finishClose` or `console-closed`) render an empty page instead of an invisible dock: a `visible` flag that unmounts `.cb-ui` and the glow. At minimum add `.cb-ui[data-leaving="true"] * { animation-play-state: paused }` and drop `will-change` when hidden. Optionally call `webview.hide()` from Rust after `window.hide()` and `webview.show()` before showing.

title: Dashboard player tracks its clip by position; a newly saved clip silently swaps the clip and discards unsaved edits
claim: Dashboard.tsx:80 `const recent = useMemo(() => clips.filter((clip) => !clip.screenshot && !clip.recording).slice(0, 3), [clips]);` and Dashboard.tsx:272 `<ClipPlayer clips={recent} index={Math.min(playing, recent.length - 1)} ...` pass a position, and ClipPlayer.tsx:86 resolves `const clip = clips[index];`. When `onClipSaved` prepends a new clip (save hotkey, a finished recording, or a friend's clip arriving), `recent[playing]` becomes a different clip; the player's reset effect (ClipPlayer.tsx:287) clears the trim and `useClipMix` drops the mix. Deletes made from the console shift the list the same way. Clips.tsx already solves this with an id playlist plus `shownId`.
fix: Track the clip by id: pass a playlist snapshot of ids, or reuse the Clips.tsx playlist logic through a shared hook.

title: Offer Accept/Decline buttons have no error handling
claim: The Accept/Decline buttons in Offers.tsx:29 and Share.tsx:298 use `action.finally(...)` with no catch, so failures are unhandled rejections with no feedback.
fix: Route the actions through a helper that shows a success toast or `lastError`.

title: Trim handles are pointer-only and have German labels in an English UI
claim: The trim handles can only be operated with a pointer, and their labels are German in an English UI: PlayerControls.tsx:252 ``aria-label={`${label} des Ausschnitts`}``.
fix: Make the handles keyboard-operable (arrow = 1 frame, shift = 1 s) and translate the labels.

title: SaveVeil canvases keep video-resolution size after every save
claim: SaveVeil's two canvases keep their size at video resolution (dom.ts `freezeFrame`) after every save: about 30 MB at 1440p and 66 MB at 4K stay allocated.
fix: Reset the canvases to 0x0 when the veil hides.

title: Friends "Latest clip" sends the newest item in one click without confirmation
claim: The Friends "Latest clip" button (Friends.tsx:135-144) sends the newest item, which may be a screenshot or a 1-hour recording, in one click mid-game with no confirmation.
fix: Add a confirm or undo, or restrict to clips.

title: FfmpegNotice countdown never counts down and Retry has no busy state
claim: FfmpegNotice's "trying again in X" text never counts down, and "Retry now" has no busy state.
fix: Tick the countdown and show a busy state on Retry.

title: `playing` stays true during save; Space calls play() on a source-less element
claim: While saving, the `pause` event never arrives (see the comment in useClipMix), so `playing` stays true, the rAF loop runs throughout, and Space calls `play()` on a source-less element, which is an unhandled rejection.
fix: Call `setPlaying(false)` in `save()`.

title: Overlay timer cleanup clears the initial array, not the current timers
claim: Overlay.tsx:112-115 `const running = timers.current; ... running.forEach(clearTimeout)` captures the initial array, so on cleanup it clears that array rather than the timers that later replaced it.
fix: Clear `timers.current` at cleanup time (read the ref when cleaning up).

title: Whole Console tree re-renders on every 1 Hz status event, even while hidden
claim: The whole Console tree re-renders on every `engine-status`, `audio-errors` and `audio-warnings` event (1 Hz each, always fresh objects), including while hidden (Console.tsx:349-353, Trouble.tsx:41-42).
fix: Compare payloads before calling setState, or skip while `hidden.current`.

title: Offers cannot distinguish same-named friends and do not strip bidi characters
claim: Offers show only `friendName` (taken from the local friend list) with no avatar, so two friends with the same display name cannot be told apart. The sender controls `t.name` and `t.game`, and bidi control characters are not stripped.
fix: Show an avatar; strip bidi control characters from sender-controlled fields.

title: Custom CSS properties require repeated `as CSSProperties` casts
claim: Inline styles setting custom CSS properties need `as CSSProperties` casts throughout; one typed helper would do.
fix: Add one typed helper for custom CSS properties.

title: Optimistic deleteClip never rolls back on failure
claim: store.ts:484 `deleteClip` removes the clip from the store optimistically and never rolls back if `api.deleteClip` throws, so the clip disappears from the UI but stays on disk and in the database until the next reload.
fix: Roll back `deleteClip` on failure and show the error.

title: Stems are not paused while the video is seeking
claim: useClipMix does not pause the stem `<audio>` elements on the video's `seeking` event, so audio from the old position keeps playing until `seeked`.
fix: Pause the stems on `seeking`.

title: Single-track clips: track gain and mute have no audible preview but are saved
claim: useClipMix.ts:128 `const separate = tracks.length > 1 && ...`; the audio-elements effect returns early when not separate, and useClipMix.ts:280 sets `video.current.volume = separate ? 0 : master;`. With one track, ClipEditor still renders a TrackRow (mute, solo, -30...+12 dB); moving it changes nothing in the preview, but Save bakes it into the file.
fix: Apply the single track's gain to the video element (attenuation via `volume`, or route the video through the same WebAudio graph for boost), or hide the row.

title: Waveform is not refreshed after a trim and is misaligned with the new timeline
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:316-326 fetches `api.clipWaveform(clipId)` with dependencies `[clipId]` only, and the URL has no cache-busting. Rust (`preview.rs`, `is_newer`) would regenerate the image, but the frontend never asks again after save or restore, so the old full-length waveform is stretched over the trimmed clip, and the WebView may serve the cached PNG under the same URL.
fix: Add `reload` (or `clip.sizeBytes`) to the dependencies and append `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, as is already done for thumbnails.

title: Frame step is hard-coded to 30 fps
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:59 `const FRAME = 1 / 30;` is used at line 478 `".": () => seek(FRAME)`. Recordings default to 60 fps, so a "single frame" step moves two frames.
fix: Carry fps in `Clip`, or derive it from `requestVideoFrameCallback` metadata.

title: Trim marks and the selection loop use currentTime instead of the presented frame
claim: Marks set while playing take `currentTime` (the audio clock), not the presented frame, and the end-of-selection loop check uses rAF plus `currentTime`.
fix: Use `rVFC.mediaTime` (requestVideoFrameCallback) for marks and for the end-of-selection loop check instead of rAF plus `currentTime`.

title: Time display and trim readout show whole seconds only
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:15 `clock()` floors to seconds, and ClipEditor shows `clock(trim.start) – clock(trim.end)`, so the handle tooltip and trim readout cannot show the sub-second precision a cut needs.
fix: Display m:ss.cc or frames.

title: Export dialog: shown size can differ from the exported target size
claim: ExportDialog.tsx:177-181 updates the target only for valid input: `setCustom(text); ... if (Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 1) setTargetMb(value);`. Typing "0.5" keeps the previous 25 MB target while the field shows 0.5. Typing "7" and then clearing the field leaves `targetMb = 7` with no preset highlighted and an empty field, yet Export is enabled.
fix: Derive `targetMb` from `custom` when it is non-empty and disable Export for invalid input.

title: Export cannot be cancelled
claim: There is no way to cancel a long export: Cancel is disabled while busy, and Rust has no cancel command.
fix: Add a cancel that kills ffmpeg.

title: Export uses the file on disk, not the unsaved selection, without saying so
claim: ExportDialog exports the file on disk, not the unsaved trim selection, and does not tell the user.
fix: Add a hint when `dirty`.

title: Player keeps reacting behind the Export dialog and the dialog follows the player's clip
claim: While ExportDialog is open, `n`/`p` still page the player. ExportDialog's `clip` prop follows the player's clip, so mid-run the dialog shows the next clip's numbers and the progress stalls.
fix: Capture the clip at mount.

title: Usage stats are on by default and a self-dismissing notice counts as consent
claim: config.rs:66 `usage_stats: true`; Setup.tsx:88 `useState(true)` then line 113 `setUsageStats(config.usageStats)` - a pre-ticked toggle on the last setup step. UsageNotice marks itself as read after 10 s with the window focused: `if (due && shownMs >= SHOWN_MS) void patchConfig({ usageStatsNoticed: true })`. telemetry.rs `send_if_due` sends a persistent UUID `id` plus `source` and `heard`. Existing users who update are opted in by a notice that dismisses itself. Under GDPR and German TTDSG §25, a pre-ticked box is not valid consent (CJEU Planet49).
fix: Make it opt-in (default `false`, toggle unticked), or at least require an explicit choice.

title: Usage notice text omits the persistent install ID and attribution fields
claim: The UsageNotice text ("the version, how many clips, which features. No content, no account.") does not mention that telemetry.rs `send_if_due` sends a persistent install UUID `id` and the attribution fields `source` and `heard`.
fix: List the install ID and the source/heard fields in the notice.

title: Console mini-player (ClipStage) has no error state
claim: In Console.tsx:1314-1340 the `
fix: Add an `onError` state ("File not found"); better, share one `useVideoTransport` hook between ClipPlayer and ClipStage.

title: Console seek shortcut can throw before metadata is loaded
claim: Console.tsx:1274 `jump(element, element.currentTime + 5)` has no `Number.isFinite(duration)` guard; `jump` computes `Math.min(x, NaN)`, so assigning `currentTime = NaN` throws a TypeError before metadata is loaded.
fix: Guard the seek with `Number.isFinite(duration)`.

title: Console player shortcuts die once the volume slider has focus
claim: Console.tsx:1270 skips all inputs including range inputs, so once the volume slider has focus every console player shortcut is dead (the opposite of the main player's choice).
fix: Share one `useVideoTransport`/shortcut logic between ClipPlayer and ClipStage with consistent input filtering.

title: ClipPlayer, ExportDialog and SharePicker have no dialog role or focus management
claim: ClipPlayer, ExportDialog and SharePicker have no dialog role, no focus trap, and do not move focus in or restore it on close.
fix: Add dialog roles and focus management (move focus in, trap, restore).

title: Overlay capability `core:event:default` lets the overlay emit events to the main window
claim: overlay.json grants `"permissions": ["core:event:default"]` with the description "only listens, controls nothing". `core:event:default` includes `allow-emit` and `allow-emit-to`, so the overlay can send `share-state`, `focus-clip`, `update-available` or `main-hidden` to the main window.
fix: Give the overlay `core:event:allow-listen` and `core:event:allow-unlisten` only.

title: Console capability grants unused window permissions and broad `core:default`
claim: The console capability grants `core:window:allow-hide/show/set-focus`, which its JavaScript never uses, and `core:default` (tray, menu and more).
fix: Drop the unused window permissions from the console capability (and restrict it to the listed command set).

title: Player's global key handler ignores menus/dialogs and hijacks keys on sliders
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:463-469 skips only text inputs, deliberately not range sliders: `(target instanceof HTMLInputElement && target.type !== "range") || target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement`. Line 499 looks up `handlers[event.key]` without checking `event.defaultPrevented` or modifier keys; line 492's Escape only respects `askingDelete` and `exporting`. Conflicts: the context menu (Menu.tsx:156) handles Escape and arrows in the capture phase with `preventDefault` but no `stopPropagation`, so Escape closes the menu and the player, and ArrowDown moves the menu selection and lowers the volume. SharePicker (Share.tsx:36), opened from the player's menu, closes on Escape and so does the player; Space, `n`, `p` act on the player behind it. ClipEditor's "Free up space" ConfirmDelete (`discarding`, ClipEditor.tsx:84) cancels on Escape and the player closes too. With a track-gain or volume slider focused, ArrowLeft/Right seek +/-5 s and ArrowUp/Down change master volume, so keyboard users cannot move any slider; Home/End are taken too. Ctrl+N/Ctrl+P page clips, Ctrl+F toggles fullscreen, and key repeat is not filtered.
fix: Return early when `event.defaultPrevented`, when Ctrl/Meta/Alt is held, or when the target is any `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `[contenteditable]` or `[role=slider]` other than the scrubber; give dialogs and menus a shared modal stack (zustand counter, or `stopPropagation` in Menu, SharePicker and ConfirmDelete) and lift `discarding` up to the player.

title: mark() does not clamp the end to duration and silently moves the start
claim: `mark()` (ClipPlayer.tsx:451-455) does not clamp the end to the duration (`Math.max(at, current.start + 0.5)`), and silently moves the start to `end - 0.5` when the playhead is past it.
fix: Clamp the end to `[start + 0.5, duration]`.

title: Slider has no focus ring
claim: The Slider uses `outline-none` (Controls.tsx:116), so there is no visible focus ring.
fix: Add a visible focus style.

title: backdrop-blur in the transparent GPU-less console costs CPU and blurs nothing
claim: `backdrop-blur` is used inside the transparent, `--disable-gpu` console (Console.tsx:642, Friends.tsx:157). It costs CPU and, as overlay.css itself notes, blurs nothing behind the window.
fix: Remove `backdrop-blur` from the console.

title: Fake RESTING mock status is the console's initial state in production
claim: Console.tsx:54-69 defines a `RESTING` mock status (`game: "ARC Raiders"`, 96 s buffered) that is used as the initial state in production too.
fix: Use null and a skeleton.

title: Installer and app exe are not Authenticode-signed, and the first install has no integrity check
claim: The `bundle.windows` block in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:63-70 has only an "nsis" section: there is no `certificateThumbprint`, `signCommand` or `timestampUrl`, so the NSIS `-setup.exe` and the app exe carry no Authenticode signature. The release pipeline produces no checksums and no provenance, and the site publishes no checksums (site/index.html:35,46 just link to `clippiboy.com/get/site`). scripts/make-probe.mjs:71 tells testers: "If Windows warns that the publisher is unknown: 'More info' and then 'Run anyway'." Minisign only protects updates; a fresh install trusts whatever asset currently sits on the latest release.
fix: Sign with Azure Trusted Signing through tauri's `bundle.windows.signCommand` (e.g. `trusted-signing-cli -e <endpoint> -a <account> -c <profile> %1`) or another OV/EV certificate; enable GitHub "immutable releases"; publish `SHA256SUMS` and `actions/attest-build-provenance` attestations and show the hash on the site; stop telling users to click through SmartScreen.

title: A workflow_dispatch "trial run" publishes a real signed release tagged `main`
claim: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-16 enables `workflow_dispatch:` under the comment `# For a trial run without a tag.`, while `:60` sets `tagName: ${{ github.ref_name }}`, `:68` `releaseDraft: false` and `:71` `includeUpdaterJson: true`. In tauri-action v0 (`src/index.ts:178`: `if (tagName && !releaseId) { ... createRelease(...) }`; `create-release.ts` calls `createRelease({ tag_name, target_commitish: commitish || context.sha, draft })`) a non-empty tagName always creates a release. On a dispatch from main, `github.ref_name` is "main", so tauri-action creates git tag `main` and publishes a non-draft release "ClippiBoy main", signed with the production updater key and carrying a `latest.json`. The comment at `:74-75` ("a workflow_dispatch trial run has no release to attach anything to") is wrong. Confirmed against tauri-action v0 source.
fix: Use `tagName: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') && github.ref_name || '' }}` (an empty tagName makes tauri-action build only), and upload trial artifacts with `actions/upload-artifact`.

title: rustls 0.23.43 has open RustSec advisories

title: Release toolchain is not reproducible (floating toolchain, no --locked)

title: Public download count includes updater traffic
claim: .github/scripts/bake-release.mjs:61-63 counts GitHub downloads of the `-setup.exe` asset and comments "The `.sig` and `latest.json` beside it are fetched by the updater, not by people, and are left out." The `/get` proxy (server/site-proxy/index.ts:61) also fetches from GitHub for bots it does not count in D1.

title: Stream Deck plugin never rediscovers the app after a connection failure

title: Stream Deck status polls overlap with no in-flight guard
claim: The plugin polls with `setInterval(…, 500)` (streamdeck/src/client.ts:116) while each request has a 2 s timeout (:88) and there is no in-flight guard.

title: Stream Deck keys are redrawn every 500 ms even when nothing changed

title: Stream Deck manifest targets end-of-life Node 20 with Debug enabled

Node 20 has been end-of-life since April 2026. `Debug: enabled` only applies in Stream Deck developer mode (`--inspect=127.0.0.1:{PORT}`) but should be removed from releases.

title: Website has no security headers
claim: The site proxy Worker (server/site-proxy/index.ts:29-43) passes GitHub Pages' headers through and only rewrites `Location`. clippiboy.com is served with no Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` or `frame-ancestors`. title: An unverified ffmpeg from the search path runs until the pinned copy is in place
claim: src-tauri/src/muxer.rs:39-49 falls back to `_ => PathBuf::from(name)` when `TOOL_DIR` is unset or the pinned file is missing. Rust's `Command` on Windows then searches the exe's own directory (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippiBoy`), then System32, then PATH, so any ffmpeg found that way runs without a hash check while the pinned download is pending ("The buffer already runs while that happens", site/index.html:191-192). This is the one gap in the otherwise end-to-end ffmpeg hash pinning.
fix: Refuse to fall back, or hash-check the fallback.

title: tools/report invokes powershell by bare name (binary planting)

title: Script-injection pattern with github.ref_name in workflow run steps

title: Third-party actions on mutable refs run alongside the updater signing key and a contents: write token

claim: README.md:759-765 documents that "the key lives under `%USERPROFILE%\.clippiboy\updater.key` with its password beside it in `updater.password`". A plaintext password sitting next to the encrypted key defeats the encryption. There is a single key with no rotation or backup plan, and README.md:750 notes it cannot be recovered if lost (part of the report's "Signing-key governance" finding).

title: GPLv3 ffmpeg is redistributed without license text or a source offer
claim: .github/workflows/ffmpeg.yml:38-39 zips only the two exes (`Compress-Archive -Path dist-ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe, dist-ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe`), dropping gyan.dev's LICENSE and README; the release notes at `:52` say only "(gyan.dev essentials build $version)". gyan.dev essentials builds are configured `--enable-gpl --enable-version3` (libx264/libx265). `scripts/make-probe.mjs --full` (:113-117) ships the same exes with no license either. Distributing GPLv3 object code requires the license and Corresponding Source, or a written offer, or equivalent access with clear directions (GPLv3 §6). Running ffmpeg as a separate process keeps the proprietary app itself out of scope, but the redistribution obligations still apply.
fix: Include `LICENSE.txt` and gyan's README in the ZIP and the release; link to or mirror the exact source and build scripts for that version; mention it in-app and on the site. Alternatively switch to an LGPL build if the GPL encoders are not needed.

title: No third-party license notices anywhere
claim: A search of `src/`, `src-tauri/src`, `src-tauri/windows` and `site/` found no third-party license or notice file or screen. The only LICENSE is the proprietary one (LICENSE:23-25 says third-party parts "stay under their own licenses"). The installer statically links about 740 crates (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC; Apache-2.0 also needs its NOTICE files), plus React, zustand, the bundled SQLite and ring. The Stream Deck plugin ships `@elgato/streamdeck`, `ws` and `zod` in `node_modules`. The site serves Inter (OFL). MIT and BSD require the copyright notice in binary distributions.
fix: Generate `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` with `cargo about` plus `license-checker` or `npm-license-crawler` in CI, bundle it as a resource, and link it from Settings → About and from the site.

There is no PR or push workflow, no `dependabot.yml`, no `rustfmt`/`clippy`/`deny` config and no `rust-toolchain.toml`. `grep '#[test]' src-tauri/src` counts 271 tests that never run in CI; `server/src/*.test.ts` and server's `tsc --noEmit` (server/package.json:9-10) never run either.

title: Manual control-port token stored in plain Stream Deck global settings
claim: The manually entered ClippiBoy control token is stored in plain Stream Deck global settings, although SDK v3 "Secrets" (Stream Deck 6.9+) exists for this purpose.
fix: Store the token with SDK v3 Secrets (Stream Deck 6.9+).

title: Recorder offers NumpadEnter and NumpadEqual, but they register Enter and the letter E system-wide
claim: KEYS (Hotkeys.tsx:83) accepts "NumpadEnter" and "NumpadEqual", and KEY_LABELS shows them as "Num Enter" / "Num =". parse_key accepts both (hotkey.rs:315-316: `"NUMPADENTER" | "NUMENTER" => Ok(NumpadEnter)`, `"NUMPADEQUAL" | "NUMEQUAL" => Ok(NumpadEqual)`). key_to_vk then maps `Code::NumpadEnter => VK_RETURN` and `Code::NumpadEqual => VK_E` (windows/mod.rs:308-309), and register() passes that VK to RegisterHotKey. Windows reports both Enter keys as VK_RETURN, so "NumpadEnter" takes the main Enter key as well. "NumpadEqual" takes the E key. risky() returns false whenever a modifier is present (Hotkeys.tsx:138), so no warning appears. apply_hotkeys checks for duplicates by string (`one.eq_ignore_ascii_case(other)`, commands.rs:211), so "Ctrl+Enter" on one action and "Ctrl+NumpadEnter" on another both pass. The second RegisterHotKey then fails with ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED, and the user is told "Ctrl+NumpadEnter is already taken by another program." (lib.rs:827-829). The clash is with ClippiBoy's own other action.
fix: Remove "NumpadEqual" from KEYS: global-hotkey 0.8.0 maps it to VK_E and there is no correct mapping. Either drop "NumpadEnter" too, or record it as "Enter" with the label "Enter", because RegisterHotKey cannot tell the two Enter keys apart. In apply_hotkeys, compare the parsed shortcuts after mapping them to their VK instead of comparing strings, and report an internal clash as "used twice", not "taken by another program".

title: risky() treats any modifier, Shift included, as safe: Shift+letter, Shift+Enter and Ctrl+C get no warning
claim: risky() is the only guard against bindings that interfere with typing. It returns false as soon as any part is in MODIFIERS: `if (keys.some((key) => MODIFIERS.includes(key))) return false;` (line 138). MODIFIERS includes "Shift" (line 125). So "Shift+S", "Shift+1", "Shift+Space", "Shift+Enter" and "Shift+Tab" produce no warning, although each one types a character or performs a text-field action. The same holds for Ctrl+C/V/X/Z/A and Alt+F4. The core registers every one of them with RegisterHotKey (windows/mod.rs:95-96), which is system-wide and takes the keystroke away from the foreground app. The warning at lines 259-264 only covers bare keys.
fix: Treat Shift-only combinations with a printable or editing key as risky, and do the same for Ctrl+Alt+<printable> (see the AltGr finding). Also warn for well-known editing and system chords: Ctrl+A/C/V/X/Z/Y, Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter, Alt+F4, Alt+Space and Alt+Tab. For example, take mods = keys.slice(0, -1) and key = keys.at(-1); return !HARMLESS.test(key) when mods is ['Shift'], or when it contains both Ctrl and Alt; then check a small deny-list.

title: Recorder stores the physical event.code but Windows matches the layout VK, so non-US layouts bind a different key than the one pressed
claim: accelerator() stores event.code (line 109). event.code names a physical key by its position on a US-QWERTY board. parse_key turns it into the Code of the same name. key_to_vk then maps that Code to the VK the key has on a US layout: Backquote=>VK_OEM_3, Semicolon=>VK_OEM_1, BracketLeft=>VK_OEM_4, Minus=>VK_OEM_MINUS, Slash=>VK_OEM_2, KeyY=>VK_Y, KeyZ=>VK_Z (mod.rs:230-252). RegisterHotKey matches virtual keys, and Windows assigns those from the active layout. On any layout where a key's VK differs from the US one, the hotkey fires on a different physical key from the one pressed. German QWERTZ (kbdgr): ^ (code Backquote) registers VK_OEM_3, which is the Ö key. ß (Minus) registers the '-' key, ´ (Equal) the '+' key, Ü (BracketLeft) the ß key, + (BracketRight) the ´ key, Ö (Semicolon) the Ü key, # (Backslash) the ^ key and '-' (Slash) the # key. The key labelled Z (KeyY) registers the key labelled Y, and the reverse. Only Ä (Quote), comma and period line up. UK (kbduk): ` (Backquote) registers VK_OEM_3, which is the apostrophe key, and ' (Quote) registers VK_OEM_7, which is the # key. keyLabel() prints the US code name ("Backquote", "Semicolon", "Y"). That is neither what is printed on the pressed key nor recognisably the key that was actually bound. Because the VK is resolved at key-press time, switching input language (Win+Space) also moves every punctuation hotkey.
fix: Record what Windows will actually match. In WebView2 on Windows, event.keyCode is the virtual key for the active layout. Map it back to the global-hotkey name whose key_to_vk yields that VK (220 -> "Backslash", 192 -> "Backquote", 90 -> "Z" and so on), and take the label from event.key or navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap(). The alternative is in Rust: convert the code to its scan code, resolve it with MapVirtualKeyExW(MAPVK_VSC_TO_VK_EX) against the current layout, and register that VK.

title: AltGr is recorded as Ctrl+Alt, and any Ctrl+Alt hotkey swallows the AltGr character on that key (@, {, \, €, Polish letters)
claim: On Windows the AltGr key is delivered as LCtrl+RAlt, and Chromium/WebView2 reports AltGr keystrokes with ctrlKey and altKey both true. accelerator() builds the modifiers from ctrlKey and altKey only (lines 104-105) and never checks getModifierState("AltGraph"), so AltGr+Q is stored as "Ctrl+Alt+Q". register() turns that into MOD_CONTROL|MOD_ALT plus VK_Q. Windows hotkey matching sees Ctrl and Alt both down while AltGr is held, so the hotkey fires whenever the user types the AltGr character on that key, and the character is consumed. risky() does not warn because the binding has modifiers (line 138).
fix: In accelerator(), ignore keystrokes with event.getModifierState("AltGraph") set, or tell the user that AltGr cannot be used. In risky(), warn for Ctrl+Alt+<printable key>, at least when navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap() or event.key shows that the key produces a character with AltGr on the current layout.

title: Hotkeys that fail to register at startup fail silently, and one such key then blocks every change to the other four
claim: At startup the error from register_hotkeys only goes to the log: `if let Err(err) = register_hotkeys(handle) { log::warn!("{err}"); }` (lib.rs:1265-1267). resume_hotkeys also only logs (commands.rs:257-258). The config keeps the combination, and the Hotkeys page has no per-row status, so it shows the key as bound. register_hotkeys returns a single error that lists every failed combination (lib.rs:823-831). apply_hotkeys treats any failure as fatal for the whole set: it rolls back all five values and re-registers the old ones (commands.rs:228-237). It does not check whether the failed combination is one the user just changed. So a combination the user never touched, but that cannot be registered, makes every later edit of any other row fail and revert.
fix: Have register_hotkeys return a result per action. In apply_hotkeys, reject and roll back only the actions whose value changed and failed. Keep unchanged actions that fail to register, and flag them instead. Show startup failures to the user, either with notify() or with a hotkey-status query that the Hotkeys page renders next to each row.

title: Default hotkeys take over some of the most common app shortcuts system-wide (Ctrl+Shift+P/R/B/S)
claim: The defaults are "Ctrl+Shift+S" (save), "Ctrl+Shift+B" (buffer), "Ctrl+Shift+P" (screenshot), "Ctrl+Shift+R" (record) and "Alt+C" (console). All of them parse, and register_hotkeys registers them with RegisterHotKey at every start. RegisterHotKey is system-wide and exclusive: the keystroke goes to ClippiBoy's hidden window and never reaches the foreground app. These chords are standard shortcuts elsewhere. Ctrl+Shift+R is hard reload in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Ctrl+Shift+P is the VS Code command palette and Firefox's private window. Ctrl+Shift+B is the bookmarks bar in Chrome and Edge and Build in VS Code and Visual Studio. Ctrl+Shift+S is Save As in VS Code, Photoshop, GIMP and Blender. toggle_recording_and_notify starts a recording regardless of whether a game is running (lib.rs:199-207). risky() never flags these because they have modifiers.
fix: Choose defaults that rarely collide, for example Alt+F9/Alt+F10-style keys or Ctrl+Alt+<F-key> as other recorders use, or leave record and screenshot unbound by default. Say during setup that the hotkeys apply in every program.

title: Recovered recordings are indexed only after every leftover is finished; a quit during a later one orphans the earlier MP4s for good
claim: lib.rs:279 `let clips = state.recover_recordings(...)` returns only after the loop at state.rs:1152-1170 has finalized every leftover. Only then does lib.rs:283-294 call `library.insert`, `store_tags`, emit `clip-saved` and show the toast. Each successful `recorder::finalize` has already deleted its work folder (`std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir)`, recorder.rs:604) before it returns. So from the moment leftover N is finalized until the insert loop runs, recording N exists only as an MP4 on disk: no work folder and no library row. Finalizing leftover N+1 takes minutes for a long recording (ffprobe counts the whole stream, then sum_tracks, then an AAC encode of every track), and a tray Quit (tray.rs:139-148 calls app.exit(0) without waiting), an update install, a crash or a Windows shutdown in that time kills the thread. On the next start leftovers() no longer sees N because its meta.json is gone, and nothing scans the clip folder: the only read_dir callers are tools.rs:295, recorder.rs:617, commands.rs:1271 and edit.rs:161. N's MP4 therefore never reaches the library, and its stems (stems::dir(id)) and thumbnail are orphaned too.
fix: Insert each recovered clip (row, tags, clip-saved, toast) as soon as its finalize returns, for example with a per-clip callback passed into recover_recordings instead of a Vec returned at the end. Better still, write the row, or a marker naming the output path in meta.json, before deleting the work folder, so a kill at any point leaves something the next start can reconcile.

title: Leftover recordings are looked for only in the current clip folder; after a folder change they are never finished or mentioned
claim: recover_recordings takes `let clip_dir = self.config_snapshot().clip_dir;` (state.rs:1149) and scans only `<that>/.recording` (recorder.rs:617). A work folder is created under whatever clip folder was configured when its recording started (recorder.rs:139). set_clip_dir (commands.rs:267-290) does not refuse a change while a recording runs, and it does not look for, move or finish leftovers in the old folder. Nothing remembers earlier clip folders for recovery: allow_existing_clip_dirs only grants them to the asset protocol. A leftover in an earlier clip folder is therefore never recovered.
fix: Recover from every clip folder that may hold leftovers: the current one, the previous config value, and the parent folders of clips in the library. Alternatively, record each work folder's path in the data dir when it is created. At minimum, check the old folder in set_clip_dir and finish its leftovers or tell the user.

title: Failed recoveries are silent and repeated in full on every start, and unrecoverable leftovers are never cleared
claim: Both failure branches of recover_recordings only `log::warn!`: 'left alone' (state.rs:1159) and 'not finished' (state.rs:1168). lib.rs:279-294 handles only the successes it gets back. There is no toast, banner or sound, no attempt counter, no backoff and no way to discard. The folder is kept on purpose (recorder.rs:552-555, 'the next start tries again'), so the whole job runs again at every launch. For a crashed recording, count_frames makes ffprobe read the entire H.264 stream (recorder.rs:540, 501-520); then sum_tracks rewrites all of mix.pcm and every track is AAC-encoded, only to fail the same way again. When autostarted this happens at Windows sign-in, while the user is starting a game. Some leftovers can never succeed: a crash before the video writer's first 1 MiB BufWriter flush (recorder.rs:49, 154) leaves video.h264 empty, so count_frames returns None ('the recording's video could not be read', recorder.rs:540-541) or 0 frames ('The recording is empty.', recorder.rs:543-545); a meta.json that does not parse is 'left alone' forever; the room shortage of VP-13 recurs every time. None of these folders (meta.json, tracks, a leftover mix.pcm) is ever removed. Each attempt also creates the game's Recordings folder through destination() before finalize (state.rs:1121, 1243-1245) and leaves it empty on failure. VP-13 covers the room guard underestimating; this finding covers recovery's error handling.
fix: Tell the user once about a failed recovery, naming the recording and the reason (for example 'needs X GB free'). Store an attempt count and the last error in meta.json and back off. Offer to delete, or delete after confirmation, folders that can never succeed (no frames, unreadable video or description). Delete mix.pcm when an attempt fails, and create the destination folder only after finalize succeeds (or prune it on failure).

title: When every recovery fails after encoding began, the closing progress event is never sent and the Record button stays disabled showing 'Saving recording… N %'
claim: lib.rs:280-282 reads `if !clips.is_empty() { recording_progress(&app, 1.0); }`, so the closing 1 goes out only when at least one recovery succeeded. finalize emits on_progress(0.1) (recorder.rs:592), and ffmpeg's out_time progress follows (muxer.rs:449-455), before encode can still fail: an ffmpeg error such as disk full while writing the MP4, 'cannot be read back', or replace_file. The store clears the bar only on share >= 1 (store.ts:289). Dashboard sets `saving = recordingSaving || recordingProgress !== null` (Dashboard.tsx:76), disables the Record button with `disabled={saving}` (line 122), and labels it 'Saving recording… N %' (lines 124-125); that label takes precedence over the Stop label even while a later recording runs. NavBar shows SavingBadge (lines 84-86). The stop path always emits 1.0 (lib.rs:241), and ipc.ts:222 documents '1 means done, either way'. The recovery path breaks that contract.
fix: After recover_recordings returns, emit recording_progress(1.0) whenever any progress was emitted (or simply always), as stop_recording_and_notify does.

title: Numpad digit hotkeys depend on NumLock, and Shift+Numpad cannot be bound (likely recorded as the bare digit)
claim: supported() accepts Numpad0-9 and NumpadDecimal by event.code (line 91), and event.code is the same whether NumLock is on or off. key_to_vk registers VK_NUMPAD0-9 and VK_DECIMAL (mod.rs:295-306). Windows produces those VKs only with NumLock on. With NumLock off, the same keys produce VK_INSERT/END/DOWN/NEXT/LEFT/CLEAR/RIGHT/HOME/UP/PRIOR and VK_DELETE. With NumLock on, Shift plus a numpad digit makes Windows inject a Shift release and send the navigation VK instead, so MOD_SHIFT+VK_NUMPADn never matches. The webview then likely sees the digit's keydown with shiftKey false, so the recorder stores a bare "NumpadN".
fix: Accept numpad digits only when event.getModifierState("NumLock") is true, or map by event.keyCode as proposed in the layout finding. Reject Shift+numpad-digit combinations and explain that Windows cannot register them.

title: Ctrl+ScrollLock, Ctrl+NumLock and Ctrl+Pause register virtual keys Windows never produces for those combinations
claim: The recorder accepts ScrollLock, NumLock and Pause with modifiers, and HARMLESS presents them as the quiet keys. Windows keyboard layouts treat NumLock and ScrollLock as multi-VK keys: with Ctrl held, NumLock produces VK_PAUSE and ScrollLock produces VK_CANCEL. Ctrl+Pause sends the Break scan code, which produces VK_CANCEL. global-hotkey registers MOD_CONTROL together with VK_NUMLOCK, VK_SCROLL or VK_PAUSE (mod.rs:294, 312, 322), which none of these key presses ever delivers.
fix: In the recorder, reject Ctrl combined with Pause, ScrollLock or NumLock and show a short reason, or record these keys by event.keyCode (VK) so the stored binding matches what Windows delivers.

title: Recovery's `live` check only excludes a registered recorder, so a recording that is being stopped can be finalized twice at once
claim: recover_recordings skips only the folder of `self.recorder` (state.rs:1150-1155) and takes no lifecycle lock. stop_recording removes the recorder from `self.recorder` in close_recording (state.rs:1059), then runs finish_recording and finalize outside the lock (state.rs:1097). That takes tens of seconds to minutes, and all the while .recording/<id>/meta.json, now with frames set, is still there. Recovery runs once, when tools::setup reaches Ready (tools.rs:156-158). That can happen at any moment after a download or a Retry, and recording is allowed during the download when ffmpeg is on PATH (state.rs:978, `!is_ready() && !available()`). If Ready lands during a stop, leftovers() returns the folder being finalized and a second finalize starts on it. The matching start window (folder created at recorder.rs:139-144, recorder registered at state.rs:1000) is harmless in practice: video.h264 is still empty there, count_frames fails, and the folder is left alone.
fix: Keep the set of work folders being finished in AppState: insert in close_recording, remove after finish_recording. recover_recordings should skip those folders, or should take its leftovers snapshot under `lifecycle` and claim each folder (for example with a lock file) before finalizing.

title: A kill between the MP4 rename and the work-folder deletion makes the next start write a second full copy of the recording
claim: finalize is not idempotent. After muxer::encode renames the finished file into place (muxer.rs:375), it still writes the stem index and runs a second ffmpeg for the thumbnail (muxer.rs:379-387). Only then does finalize delete the work folder (recorder.rs:604). A kill in that window leaves both the finished MP4 and .recording/<id>/meta.json. The next start finalizes the folder again. finish_recording names the output with the current time (destination() uses jiff::Zoned::now(), state.rs:1226-1231), so it writes a second complete copy beside the first instead of over it. Only the second copy gets a library row. The first, the same recording at gigabytes in size, is never indexed and never removed by deleting the clip. Secondary path: if remove_dir_all fails with meta.json still present (it only logs a warning, recorder.rs:604-606), the clip has already been indexed, so the next start re-finalizes it and INSERT OR REPLACE (clips.rs:100) resets the row's title, description, favorite and edit.
fix: Make the output name deterministic for a work folder: derive it from meta.id or created_at, or save the chosen output path in meta.json before encoding. On recovery, if that output already exists and probes to the expected length, skip the encode and just index it. Use deleting meta.json, or renaming the folder, as the explicit commit point.

title: A crashed recording is recovered with only the game and friends from its start, and is named after the time of recovery
claim: meta.json gets its game and friends when the recording starts (state.rs:1029-1045, game_for(ZERO)). Only Recorder::finish updates the game (recorder.rs:343-351). Nothing rewrites meta.json when a game is detected during the recording, even though track_game updates buffering_game then (state.rs:681-683) and the code says a game detected half way should still claim the recording (recorder.rs:333-335). After a crash finish never ran, so the recovered clip carries the start-time game, or none. lib.rs:291 deliberately adds no current friends. destination() names the file with the recovery time, not meta.created_at. created_at, tags from meta.friends, and the current clip folder are otherwise used correctly.
fix: Rewrite meta.json (game and friends) when the held game changes while recording, and name a recovered file from meta.created_at.
